title: Smart prospecting
summary: Learn how data and technology transform wealth management marketing in our latest whitepaper and solution sheet. Learn more today.
body_text: Introduction The current landscape of wealth management is dramatically changing due to three key factors: the aftereffects of the pandemic, the growth of the mass affluent market segment and, the HENRYs (high earners, not rich yet) who will soon be driving a huge generational transfer of wealth. Many U.S. consumers who do not have money now will have significant assets in the near future. This white paper discusses how these market changes are driving the need for wealth management companies to adopt a holistic data-driven approach to prospecting. Further, we will present how firms will benefit from a personalized, omnichannel strategy, reaching prospects and clients at the right time, place, and frequency to build trusted relationships. Embracing the evolution of wealth management to capture the next generation of investors The work of wealth management has been dramatically and forever altered since the pandemic. Investor attitudes, behaviors, and expectations have been reshaped by monetary policy changes and the widespread accessibility of AI and other technologies. Additionally, the industry sees two new market segments that are gaining ground: the mass affluent segment and the upcoming transfer of generational wealth. The mass affluent. According to the UBS Global Wealth Report 2023, the mass affluent segment now represents 26% of the U.S. population, and has between $100,000 and $1 million liquid assets and an annual household income above $75,000. A smaller, but significant portion of this segment are HENRYs, earning over $100,000 annually but with a net worth under $1 million. Currently, HENRYs are spending most of their income on living expenses. In the future, due to their careers, education, and other underlying factors, they are expected to experience a rapid and significant velocity of asset growth within a relatively short timeframe. The great wealth transfer. According to a report by Cerulli, an asset management consulting firm, an estimated $84.4 trillion in wealth will be transferred by 2045, with $72.6 trillion to be passed on to heirs. A whole new generation of consumers, possibly unfamiliar with wealth management, will need to find and work with an advisor to manage and protect their inherited assets. In addition to the growing mass affluent market and coming generational wealth transfer, consumer behavior in general is changing, along with other industry dynamics: Shifting investor behavior: Widespread accessibility of brokerage platforms such as E*TRADE and Robinhood has led to a shift in where and how investors wish to manage their wealth. Traditional wealth management firms now must compete with the ease of accessibility and improved visibility into investment performance these digitally native firms offer. An EY report indicates Millennials are more than twice as likely (73%) than Boomers (29%) to switch between providers, to move assets between firms or to begin working with new wealth managers. They are also far more likely (49%) than the global average (33%) to have sought independent professional advice in response to external shocks. Digital transformation: Younger generations entering their wealth accumulation years often prefer digital and self-service solutions for asset management. Technological and operational advancements will be essential to meet the expectations of retail investors, who are now accustomed to seamless customer experiences and improved accessibility. Addressing the talent gap: The current advisor workforce is retiring soon, underscoring the urgent need for new talent that can get up to speed quickly. A Cerulli report projects that 36% of the industry's workforce will retire within the next decade, impacting nearly 40% of advisory assets. “Advances in technology, shifting demographics, and generational wealth transfers are changing the way wealth managers and advisors must think about prospecting for new clients and expanding relationships with current ones. Data-driven prospecting and analytics are key to success as the industry digitizes and evolves. Genesys has aligned with leading partners to further extend Genesy Cloud’s front office capabilities. EXL’s capabilities to provide hyper-personalization will help transform how wealth managers and advisors think about marketing, relationship building, and client retention while relying upon Genesys Cloud’s proven capabilities in voice and digital interactions.” – David Porter Managing Director of Financial Services, Genesys Market changes are driving a new approach to lead generation. Historically, prospecting for new wealth management clients relied on personal relationships, the one-on-one marketing of “I know a guy.” While today’s corporate lead generation programs have moved beyond this, prospecting still remains a one-dimensional activity. Companies buy or generate an email list, host a webinar or podcast, and then have a call center team warm up leads for further engagement. At some point, prospective clients are assigned to a financial advisor or private banker to continue building the relationship to nurture. None of these activities are personalized to the prospective client. Beyond broad demographic parameters, everyone is treated relatively the same. Yet today, a whole new universe of data is available to wealth management marketers. By utilizing data-driven technology, companies can quickly and accurately find leads to create a more personalized, targeted prospecting approach. Digital solutions based on AI and machine learning allow wealth management firms to see and address client needs in a whole new way. Marketers can meet each consumer in their channel of choice and provide a financial product that addresses their needs in that moment such as mortgage lending, debt consolidation, or asset structure for a retirement account. Advancements in cloud infrastructure, customer experience platforms, machine learning, and AI are transforming the business of wealth management. Utilizing technology innovation is paramount for wealth management firms to capture the next generation of investors and provide more personalized, efficient, and effective services to their clients. The adoption of these innovative technologies enables advisors to deliver hyper-personalized services at scale by establishing a deeper understanding of their clients’ needs and preferences. By leveraging data and technology, wealth management firms can unlock the full potential of the mass affluent and HENRY segments, while also preparing for the upcoming wealth transfer and the evolving needs of a new generation of investors. Harnessing the power of data analytics is the key to success in this generational shift. Wealth advisors can gain deeper insights into client behaviors, preferences, and financial goals, enabling them to deliver tailored recommendations that resonate with individual needs. This enhances the quality of client interactions and strengthens the advisor's credibility and competitiveness in the marketplace. – Gray Ditsler Product Manager, Performance Marketing for Wealth EXL Leveraging data-driven technology to find HENRYs. Advanced data technology platforms now allow financial institutions to monitor, detect, and signal client life changes based on life stage, online and offline behavior, and account transactions. This process, known as intelligent prospecting, aggregates data from various sources and identifies patterns and trends in financial behavior that indicate a customer's progression towards the mass affluent category. Rapid asset growth is traditionally associated with major life events such as business sales, promotions, and inheritances. By analyzing demographic data, transaction histories, and market trends, wealth management companies can pinpoint segments with the highest propensity for asset growth. With real-time monitoring, firms can continuously track transactions and financial activities to update predictions and signal changes promptly. Using a connected outreach ecosystem: the power of precision. Once a mass affluent or HENRY prospect has been uncovered, wealth management firms can leverage their connected ecosystem to deliver hyper-personalized, client-centric advice at scale. A customized strategy could be developed based on the underlying circumstances of each individual or household. Tailored recommendations and communications that resonate with each client can be created that match a client’s demographics, financial goals, and risk appetite. Utilizing omnichannel marketing, firms can ensure consistent messaging across various platforms such as social media, websites, and email campaigns. By integrating customer data and utilizing personalized communications, wealth management marketers can ultimately build trust and ongoing engagement. Empowering the next generation of wealth management advisors. Data-driven technology solutions are reshaping the wealth management industry and not a moment too soon. With an aging population of advisors retiring, firms are losing their most experienced and trusted professionals. The next generation of advisors coming on board will be the ones to address this incoming market of mass affluent and new generational wealth. These advisors will need to be trained quickly and given the technology resources needed to be successful in growing their books of business. title: Melatonin Hangover: Unmasking the Unpleasant Side Effects
summary: Unmask the effects of a melatonin hangover. Explore insights into the potential drawbacks and how to manage them. Dive into our comprehensive guide now!
body_text: Melatonin’s like your body’s own sleep DJ - it sets the vibe, tells you when to fall sleep, when to get up. But you might have experienced popping a melatonin supplement and, well, things don't always go the way you envisioned the next morning. Next thing you know, you’re waking up groggy, dragging yourself around like you pulled an all-nighter (when all you did was try to get a decent sleep). This is what people refer to as the notorious “melatonin hangover”. You try to reach for better sleep, but end up with more brain fog than before the next day. We asked Dr. Suzanne Gorovoy, Sleep Expert, Clinical Psychologist, and Behavioral Sleep Medicine Specialist, about melatonin’s next-day effects. She explains: “Next-morning grogginess is a hallmark of melatonin hangover, especially with high or mistimed doses.” Ultimately, melatonin can leave you feeling hungover the next day, equivalent to having been out drinking all night and then waking up feeling brain fog. We've been there and we're here to share more about this melatonin hangover. Unpacking the Melatonin Hangover Ever wake up feeling like you’re dragging a sack of bricks around, even though you technically got enough sleep? That’s what we call the “ melatonin hangover .” It’s like your brain’s still wrapped up in a sleepy burrito and just refuses to come out. Melatonin hangover refers to the persistent drowsiness and cognitive impairment experienced upon awakening despite adequate sleep duration following melatonin supplementation. This phenomenon occurs when exogenous melatonin administration disrupts natural circadian rhythm regulation, resulting in delayed sleep-to-wake transitions. Contributing factors to melatonin hangover include excessive dosage, individual sensitivity variations, and circadian rhythm desynchronization. When melatonin levels remain elevated beyond the natural wake time, the sleep-wake cycle becomes dysregulated, leading to the characteristic symptoms of melatonin hangover: reduced alertness and cognitive performance upon awakening. Defining the Morning Grogginess A melatonin hangover shows up as that groggy, foggy feeling you get in the morning—what doctors call sleep inertia. You might notice your thinking feels cloudy, your movements are slower, and your brain just doesn't seem to "turn on" as quickly as usual. This happens because your brain is still partially stuck in sleep mode, even though your body is awake. When you take melatonin, sometimes it sticks around longer than it should. Instead of clearing out by morning, elevated melatonin levels can extend that drowsy transition period between sleep and being fully awake. This creates a disconnect where your body might be up and moving, but your mind is still catching up—that's the classic sign of melatonin hangover. Think of melatonin hangover as your nervous system being caught between two states. While you're physically awake and going through the motions, your brain is still operating in a sleepy mode. This mismatch affects your ability to think clearly, pay attention, and perform at your best during those crucial morning hours. Rather than helping you wake up naturally, leftover melatonin from the night before can actually work against your body's natural wake-up signals. This throws off the delicate balance between feeling sleepy and feeling alert, which is exactly what creates that melatonin hangover effect. Duration of Post-Sleep Impact Melatonin hangover affects everyone differently - some people barely notice it, while others feel significantly impaired for several hours. Most people experience melatonin hangover symptoms for about 2 to 4 hours after waking up, but this varies based on how much melatonin you took, how sensitive you are to it, and how your body processes it. The impact of melatonin hangover can range from mild mental fuzziness to feeling genuinely impaired at work or during daily activities. If you're taking higher doses or you're particularly sensitive to melatonin, you're more likely to experience a stronger, longer-lasting melatonin hangover. Melatonin hangover typically fades gradually as your body clears the remaining melatonin from your system, similar to how other medications wear off over time. How quickly this happens depends largely on your individual metabolism—some people process melatonin faster than others, which directly affects how long their melatonin hangover lasts. Understanding your personal melatonin hangover pattern can help you and your healthcare provider adjust your dose and timing to minimize these morning effects. Researchers are actively studying what makes some people more prone to melatonin hangover than others, working toward more personalized approaches that provide better sleep without the unwanted morning grogginess. Common Symptoms Explored Individuals experiencing a melatonin hangover often report a constellation of symptoms akin to the groggy aftershock of insufficient sleep. Notable among these are fatigue, mood disturbances, and impaired cognitive function, attributes which can obstruct one's routine endeavors and degrade one’s quality of life if not promptly addressed and managed. Furthermore, these consequences on wakefulness and mood regulation can skew personal perception of efficacy, frequently leading to an erroneous reduction or termination of use. Proper education on these potential side effects is essential to ensure adherence to prescribed regimens and avoidance of abrupt cessation that may rebound to disturbed sleep cycles. Cognitive Function Decline Melatonin's efficacy in promoting sleep may come at the cost of next-day cognitive sluggishness, impacting processes such as memory retention and decision-making. Memory Impairment: Difficulty in recalling information, which can influence both short-term and long-term memory functions. Reduced Alertness: A lowered ability to remain attentive, possibly impairing reaction times and vigilance. Executive Dysfunction: Challenges in planning, organizing, and executing tasks that require complex cognitive engagement. The physiological interactions leading to these cognitive disruptions are under scrutiny, with an emphasis on dosing and individual metabolic differences. Moreover, such decline, if persistent, necessitates a review of melatonin usage, balancing therapeutic benefits against potential drawbacks for cognitive health. Physical Side Effects The aftermath of melatonin consumption can manifest as a series of physical symptoms. Drowsiness: A pervasive sense of sleepiness that extends into the waking hours. Headache: Experiencing mild to severe head pain, indicative of melatonin's cranial vascular effects. Dizziness: A sense of unsteadiness or loss of balance, which may relate to the central nervous system's response. Nausea: An unsettling stomach discomfort, potentially linked to melatonin's interaction with digestive processes. These adverse effects cast a shadow on melatonin's role as a facilitator of restorative sleep. It's crucial to underline that individual susceptibility to these side effects can vary, influenced by factors such as dosage and frequency of use. Dosage and Its Consequences Here’s the thing about melatonin gummies that nobody really tells you: the dose actually matters… a lot. You’d think popping one would just knock you out and, boom!..sweet dreams. But it’s not so simple. Take too little and you might as well be chewing on a gummy bear for all the good it does. Zero effect, maybe just a placebo nap. But if you go all-in and take too much? Welcome to the “melatonin hangover.” Heavy eyelids, feeling like your brain’s stuck in molasses, and wandering around like you’re in some kind of mental fog the next day. There’s nothing worse than trying to function at work while your brain’s still hitting the snooze button. Guessing your melatonin dose is asking for trouble. The smart approach is getting guidance from a healthcare professional who understands sleep medicine—not relying on casual advice from friends or online forums. Finding the right dose makes the difference between waking up refreshed and dealing with a melatonin hangover the next day. Proper melatonin dosing requires precision for good reason. When the dose is too low, you might not get the sleep benefits you're looking for, making the supplement essentially useless. But when you take too much, you significantly increase your chances of experiencing unwanted side effects, including the dreaded melatonin hangover. Taking too much melatonin can seriously impact how you function the next day. Higher doses often lead to prolonged drowsiness that extends well into the morning, making it harder to think clearly and stay alert when you need to be productive. This is why working with a healthcare provider to find your optimal melatonin dose is so important—they can help you get the sleep benefits while minimizing the risk of a melatonin hangover that leaves you feeling worse than before you started taking it. The goal is finding that sweet spot where melatonin helps you sleep better without creating morning grogginess that interferes with your daily life. Professional guidance ensures you're using melatonin safely and effectively, rather than playing a guessing game with your sleep and next-day performance. General Dosing Guidelines Most sleep medicine experts recommend starting with a very low dose—typically between 0.5 to 1 mg, taken about 1-3 hours before your desired bedtime. This might seem surprisingly low compared to what you see on store shelves (which often contain 3-10 mg), but research suggests that lower doses are often more effective and cause fewer side effects. Many people find that 0.5-3 mg is sufficient for sleep support. The "more is better" approach often backfires with melatonin, leading to that groggy melatonin hangover feeling the next day. Factors That Affect Your Ideal Dose Your optimal dose depends on several factors: Age (older adults often need less) Body weight and metabolism Sensitivity to melatonin Other medications you're taking The specific sleep issue you're addressing Whether you're dealing with jet lag or general sleep difficulties The Smart Approach Start low and adjust gradually if needed, giving each dose level at least a week to assess its effects. If 0.5 mg doesn't help after a week, you might try 1 mg, then 2 mg if necessary. Many people find their sweet spot somewhere in this range. Finding the Right Balance Getting melatonin dosing right takes some attention to how your body specifically responds to it. The key is making small adjustments with professional guidance, so you can improve your sleep without ending up with a melatonin hangover the next day. There's no universal "perfect dose" because everyone's body handles melatonin differently. Your age, weight, other medications, and individual sensitivity all play a role in how melatonin affects you and how long it stays in your system. The smart approach is starting with the smallest effective dose and only increasing if needed, while watching for signs that you might be taking too much—like excessive drowsiness or morning grogginess. Factors like your metabolism, current health conditions, and other medications can all influence how your body processes melatonin. When you combine the right melatonin dose with good sleep habits, like a consistent bedtime routine, you're more likely to support your natural sleep-wake cycle without carrying that sedated feeling into the next day. Finding your optimal balance requires patience, careful attention to how you feel, and honest communication with your healthcare provider. This collaborative approach helps you avoid the pitfalls while getting the most benefit from melatonin. Risks of Overconsumption Taking too much melatonin can seriously backfire on your sleep goals. Instead of waking up refreshed, you might find yourself dealing with intense brain fog, mood changes, and that disorienting "where am I?" feeling that defeats the whole purpose of trying to sleep better. While melatonin has a reputation as a gentle sleep aid, overdoing it can cause problems that are the opposite of what you're trying to achieve. Grogginess, mood disruptions, and confusion are common when people take more than their body can handle effectively. Higher doses make melatonin hangover symptoms much worse. Taking too much can also mess with your hormone balance, especially if you're consistently overdoing it. This can create a frustrating cycle where you feel tired during the day, leading you to think you need even more melatonin, which just makes the problem worse. Chronic overuse puts unnecessary stress on your body's natural systems. When you regularly flood your system with excess melatonin, you risk disrupting your hormonal balance and throwing off your internal clock. This can lead to more health issues down the road that go well beyond just poor sleep. Mitigating the Melatonin Fog To minimize that cloudy, groggy feeling often called "melatonin fog," stick to evidence-based dosing recommendations. Start with the smallest dose that works and pay attention to how it affects your sleep before considering any increases. If you're still experiencing persistent tiredness or confusion, talk to a healthcare professional about adjusting your dose or exploring other sleep solutions that won't leave you feeling impaired in the morning. Good sleep hygiene practices work hand-in-hand with melatonin to reduce hangover effects. Maintaining a regular sleep schedule and creating an environment that promotes restful sleep can significantly improve your results and reduce unwanted morning grogginess. Smart, measured use of melatonin combined with professional guidance when needed gives you the best shot at avoiding the hangover effect while still getting the sleep benefits you're looking for. Timing Your Intake We asked Dr. Samantha Domingo, Sleep Expert and Clinical Health Psychologist, how to prevent melatonin-related grogginess. She says: “To avoid this, take it at the same time nightly, ideally 60 to 90 minutes before bed, and start with a microdose.” What she means is consistency and lower doses can help your body respond better to melatonin, making it more likely to support healthy sleep without the unwanted morning fog. Avoid late-night dosing: Melatonin taken too close to morning can disrupt the subsequent wake cycle. Consider pharmacokinetics: The time it takes for melatonin to peak in your bloodstream varies; typically, it peaks after 60 minutes. Understand your chronotype : Knowing whether you are a morning person or a night owl can influence the ideal timing for your melatonin intake. To minimize the risk of a melatonin hangover, align your intake with your natural sleep-wake cycle. Proper timing can enhance the efficacy of melatonin and help prevent next-day grogginess. Alternative Remedies and Practices As we venture beyond pharmacological interventions, consider the merits of sleep-hygiene optimization , which encompasses establishing a consistent bedtime routine, ensuring a quiet and comfortable sleeping environment, and avoiding exposure to stimulating electronic devices before sleep. Cultivating mindfulness through meditation may support relaxation and facilitate a smoother transition into sleep without chemical aid. Physical exercises, such as yoga or light stretching, can alleviate anxiety and promote physiological readiness for rest, potentially reducing reliance on sleep aids. Establishing a regular pattern of exposure to natural light during the day helps to recalibrate the circadian rhythm, subsequently improving sleep quality and diminishing the potential for sleep aid hangovers. In cases where stress is a significant contributor to sleep disruption, psychological therapies, including cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) for insomnia, can effectively address underlying issues and enhance sleep without pharmacological dependencies. Lastly, nutritional interventions, focusing on a balanced diet rich in sleep-promoting nutrients such as magnesium and omega-3 fatty acids, can naturally foster a restorative sleep environment in the body. Start Sleeping Better With Sleep Reset Today! If you're looking for a drug-free way to get better sleep, the Sleep Reset program can help. We use CBT-I principles to help you fall asleep and stay asleep all night. Our free sleep quiz can help you identify the underlying causes of your sleep problems, so you can find the best solution for you. Our program does not rely on harmful pills, melatonin or supplements – which means no grogginess, dependency, or long-term health risks. Instead of relying on quick fixes, we use proven techniques to address the root causes of your sleep issues and give you the long-term tools to manage your sleep. Our dedicated sleep coach will help you via daily text to provide accountability, support, and guidance. The Sleep Reset program is available on iOS and Android. Instead of throwing more melatonin at your insomnia and waking up groggy, how about trying something that actually tackles the root of the problem? There’s a quick (and free) sleep quiz to figure out what’s messing with your sleep. Once you’re in, their sleep coaches, real humans, not robots, set you up with a plan that actually helps. So, ditch the zombie mornings and let Sleep Reset help you remember what real rest feels like. title: What Are We Proposing?

body_text: Odyssey has submitted an unsolicited request asking the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) , an agency within the U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI) to consider holding a lease sale that would authorize marine mineral exploration in a carefully selected offshore area off of the Virginia coast. Following its review of the request, BOEM initiated the first step in the process by publishing a Request for Information and Interest (RFI) to gather feedback from interested stakeholders. On the condition that BOEM grants a lease and it is awarded to Odyssey, we would follow a structured exploration program under BOEM oversight and the applicable environmental review processes required under NEPA in order to confirm whether heavy mineral sands (HMS) are present in concentrations suitable for future development. Partnering with Great Lakes Dredge & Dock (GLDD) , the largest U.S. dredging company, we intend to proceed with a four-phased approach, each clearly defined and only allowing advancement once regulatory approvals are secured and environmental reviews are completed. All work would be conducted in coordination with relevant agencies, with opportunities for public involvement throughout the review process. Phase 1: Gathering Baseline Information Phase 1 is intended to address any data gaps identified through collaboration with BOEM. We would conduct high-resolution sonar mapping of the seafloor, shallow sediment sampling to understand geology and biology, and conduct surveys to identify any cultural or archaeological resources or potential hazards. These preliminary activities use low-energy acoustic tools commonly used in oceanographic research and are generally expected to have localized and temporary effects, subject to BOEM review. Per the Jones Act (Merchant Marine Act of 1920), operations, if approved, would be conducted using U.S.-built, U.S.-flagged research vessels crewed by U.S. citizens. Phase 2: Defining the Resource Phase 2 covers the Delineation Plan, which is a BOEM-approved scientific program that maps where minerals are located, how deep, and whether they are recoverable and commercially viable. Anticipated to last approximately 12 months, this phase includes multibeam sonar and sub-bottom profiling, magnetometer surveys, sediment samples, and lab testing. These tools and surveys are meant to detect hazards and understand mineral grade processing behavior, while also identifying any archaeological sites or unexploded ordnance (UXO), though initial desktop reviews have not identified known cultural resources or UXO sites within the outlined area. Phase 3: Pilot Testing Phase 3 involves pilot testing if the Delineation data shows promising HMS resources. We would request BOEM approval for a Pilot Testing Plan that then would undergo environmental review and public comment prior to approval. The testing plan involves collecting a bulk amount of material to evaluate dredging performance and mineral processing methods. Pilot testing would occur in small, controlled areas. Potential environmental effects would be evaluated through BOEM's review process, with mitigation measures applied as appropriate. Phase 4: Commercial Development Planning Phase 4 is the final phase, containing commercial development planning and production. This phase is only considered if scientific data confirms the resource; environmental review supports proceeding, and BOEM approves a detailed Dredging Plan through a rigorous NEPA review process. A Science First, Phased Approach It is important to reiterate that this phase program is exploration based, with the goal of researching and gathering data to confirm the presence of HMS in volumes large enough for development in the future. All activities would be subject to regulatory oversight, environmental review, and approval requirements designed to ensure activities are undertaken responsibly.

title: Intapp now enforces your ethical walls inside Harvey
summary: The Harvey and Intapp Walls integration is now generally available. Sync your existing Walls policies into Harvey and enforce them automatically across Assistant, Vault, and Spaces.
body_text: The Harvey and Intapp integration is now live. The Harvey and Intapp Walls integration is now generally available. Confidentiality risk has been one of the biggest barriers to AI adoption at law firms, and today that changes. Intapp Walls and Harvey are now integrated, letting firms sync their existing Walls policies directly into Harvey and enforce them automatically across Harvey Assistant, Vault, and Spaces. Here’s why it matters for firms deciding how far to take AI. More than 70 of the Am Law 100 rely on Walls to enforce information barriers, and it has become the industry standard for governing confidential information. For two decades, compliance teams have configured the policies, calibrated enforcement, and earned sign-off on the infrastructure that screens lawyers from conflicting matters. Then the firm deploys a legal AI platform, and those walls stop at the edge of the systems they were built for. Inside the AI tool, governance falls back to lawyer discipline. AI has opened a compliance gap that firms did not plan for, and the numbers show how wide it already is. 83% of lawyers use AI in 2026 Source: Bloomberg Law, June 2026 5% of law firm leaders trust their current AI quality controls Source: Global Legal Post, 2026 legal sector outlook study Earlier this year, Harvey and Intapp announced a partnership to close that gap. Today, after an early access period with a select group of firms, the integration is generally available. Lawyers need their professional responsibility standards to follow them into every tool they use. This partnership ensures the same ethical walls they trust are enforced inside Harvey. Winston Weinberg, CEO, Harvey What actually goes wrong Consider a lawyer screened off a litigation matter because the firm represents the opposing party. In the document management system, the screen holds. They cannot open those files. Then they open an AI assistant, pull matter documents into a shared workspace, and invite a colleague who happens to be walled off from that matter. The information has just moved through a channel that the firm’s walls never see. The screen did its job in the DMS. The exposure reappeared one layer up. An AI-enabled lateral conflict, a privileged-information leak through a shared workspace, or an outside counsel guideline (OCG) violation that surfaces in audit becomes a partner-room event, and every new AI tool the firm adopts widens the surface where it can happen. Native AI controls handle part of the picture. Every AI platform ships with controls for authentication and workspace permissions, and they handle those jobs well for a single tool. Ethical walls ask for something more specific: lateral-hire screens, matter-level confidentiality, waiver-driven restrictions, and controls on material nonpublic information (MNPI), enforced consistently and logged for audit across every system the firm runs. Secure a second AI tool with native controls alone and the policies begin again in a separate console, rebuilding tool by tool the fragmentation the firm spent years removing. How Intapp Walls and Harvey work together With the integration, firms sync their existing Intapp Walls policies directly into Harvey, and Harvey enforces them automatically across Harvey Assistant, Vault, and Spaces — the surfaces lawyers use to research, draft, and analyze every day. Harvey inherits walls directly from the source. It never creates, changes, or deletes them. It enforces the policies Intapp Walls already manages. When access to a resource cannot be confirmed, Harvey blocks it. For compliance teams, that means one authoritative set of policies, zero parallel administration, and full consistency between what the firm’s system of record says and what Harvey enforces. Enforce your walls automatically: When a wall is created or updated in Intapp Walls, Harvey syncs it automatically. Lawyers see only the matters Walls has authorized. Firms can extend Harvey to every practice group while the walls they already validated apply from the first day, with no new round of IT configuration or compliance review. Stay audit-ready from day one: Every enforcement event traces back to both systems. If a matter’s confidentiality is ever challenged, the conflicts team can produce an unbroken record showing exactly which wall policy governed Harvey’s behavior, down to the sync timestamp. This gives the firm the evidence it needs for internal stakeholders, regulators, and courts. Keep collaboration governed: Your walls follow the work automatically. Self-maintaining walls add and remove people based on time or document activity, and matter teams can request and approve access within policy, without a compliance ticket for every change. Sensitive matters stay protected while the firm keeps moving. One policy layer for every AI tool Intapp Walls enforces one firm-wide policy set across Harvey, Microsoft Copilot, and Intapp Celeste today, with additional platforms on the roadmap. Firms define a barrier once and it applies everywhere, added to each new tool through simple API configuration. Adding the fourth AI tool looks like adding the first. As the firm’s AI footprint grows, the governed layer grows with it, and the audit trail stays in one place. Firms do not have to bet on which AI tool wins. Walls extends to whichever ones they choose. Make firm-wide rollout certifiable For most firms the question now is how to move from a controlled pilot to firm-wide AI. The prize is real, and firms expect AI to deliver it. 240 hours saved per lawyer each year, anticipated $19K in value unlocked per lawyer each year, anticipated 2x more likely to grow revenue for firms with a visible AI strategy Sources: Thomson Reuters, Future of Professionals 2025; ACEDS + Secretariat 2025 Legal AI Report. Capturing that upside is a hard step: 88% of AI proofs of concept never reach production, and governance is often where they stall. Deployment waits on a general counsel who will certify firm-wide rollout only once the controls are provable. Intapp Walls is what makes that certification possible. Your firm has already done the hard part. The policies exist, compliance has validated them, and they govern every other system the firm runs. Putting that same infrastructure to work inside AI tools turns firm-wide rollout into an extension of controls the firm already trusts, so the decision to expand AI access rests on walls the firm has already validated.See how it works in practice. Activate ethical walls in Harvey with Intapp The integration is available exclusively for Intapp Walls for AI, the cloud version of Intapp Walls. If your firm is already on it, you can activate now. title: Powering AI Centers with AI Spines
summary: Leaf-spine architectures have been widely deployed in the cloud, a model pioneered and popularized by Arista since 2008.
body_text: Leaf-spine architectures have been widely deployed in the cloud, a model pioneered and popularized by Arista since 2008. Arista’s flagship 7800 chassis embodies core cloud principles – industry leading scale, a lossless fabric, ultra-low latency, powerful observability and built-in resiliency. It has evolved into the Universal AI Spine, delivering massive scale, predictable performance, and high‑speed interface support. The Arista 7800 is equipped with powerful features such as Virtual Output Queuing (VOQ) to eliminate head‑of‑line blocking and large buffers to absorb AI microbursts and prevent PFC storms. Changing the face of AI Networking Accelerators have intensified network needs that continue to grow and evolve. AI networks of tomorrow must handle 1000X or more workloads for both training and inference frontier models. For training, the key metric is job completion time (JCT) the amount of time an XPU cluster takes to complete a job. For inference, the key metric is different; it is the time taken to process tokens. Arista has developed a comprehensive AI suite of features to uniquely manage AI and cloud workload fidelity across the diversity, duration, and size of traffic flows and patterns. To address this, Arista’s Accelerated Networking portfolio consists of three families of Etherlink Spine-Leaf fabric that we successfully deploy in scale up, scale out and scale across network designs. AI Spines to the Rescue The explosive growth in bandwidth demands from XPUs has driven the evolution of the traditional spine into a new class of purpose-built AI spines. Three major factors are contributing to scale. Bisectional bandwidth growth : Bisection bandwidth is essentially the throughput across the “out and across” the network. As workloads become more complex and more distributed, the cross-fabric bandwidth must scale smoothly as additional devices are added to avoid bottlenecks and preserve performance. Collective degradation : As you scale up or out, collective communication can become a bottleneck. The system must prevent performance from falling off a cliff as more nodes participate. Sustained real-world XPU utilization (~ 75%, not 50%). The goal isn’t a theoretical peak. It’s about keeping the system doing useful work at scale, consistently, under production-like conditions. Adapting to Massive Scale of AI Centers For ultra large-scale AI applications, requiring tens of thousands of XPUs to interconnect within a data center, and in some cases as many as 100k parallel XPUs, Arista’s universal leaf-spine design offers the simplest, most flexible, and scalable architecture to support AI workloads. Arista EOS enables intelligent real‑time load balancing that accounts for actual network utilization to uniformly distribute traffic and avoid flow collisions. Its advanced telemetry capabilities, such as AI Analyzer and Latency Analyzer, give network operators clear insight into optimal configuration thresholds, ensuring XPUs can sustain line‑rate throughput across the fabric without packet loss. Depending on the scale of the AI cluster, AI leaf options could range from fixed AI platforms to high-capacity 7800-series modular platforms. Arista’s Latest AI Spine - 7800R4 Arista’s 7800R4 is a game‑changing alternative to traditional disaggregated leaf–spine designs, which rely on a fully routed L3 EVPN/VXLAN fabric and require many separate boxes connected across multiple racks. Troubleshooting is no longer a single-layer exercise; it requires navigating multiple control-plane and data-plane layers, as well as overlay and underlay interactions. Even routine diagnostics can become time-consuming and error-prone. The 7800R4 AI spine platform eliminates the unnecessary software complexity, elevated power consumption, and operational overhead inherent in disaggregated leaf–spine designs. Instead, it provides an elegant, integrated solution that is significantly easier to troubleshoot, on board and helps alleviate congestion, ensuring reliable job completion times and performance. The 7800 AI spine consolidates the control plane, power, cooling, data forwarding, and management functions into a single unified system. Customers now benefit from a centralized point for configuration, monitoring, and diagnostics—directly addressing one of the most important customer priorities in AI workloads: operational simplicity with predictable RDMA performance, as shown below. Designed for Resilience The 7800 fabric is inherently self-healing. The internal links connecting ingress silicon, fabric modules, and egress silicon are designed with built-in speed-up and are continuously monitored during operation. If a fabric link experiences a fault, it is automatically removed from the scheduling path and reinstated only after it has recovered. This automated resilience reduces operational burden and ensures consistent and predictable system behavior. The 7800 is engineered for high availability, incorporating redundant supervisor modules, fabric cards, and power supplies. All major components—fabric modules, line cards, power supplies, and supervisors—are field-replaceable, ensuring rapid recovery from hardware faults and minimizing service disruption. This offers a level of elegance that disaggregated boxes struggle to match. It employs a scheduled VOQ fabric with hierarchical buffering, enabling packets to move efficiently from ingress to egress without head-of-line blocking or packet collisions. Because buffering occurs at ingress, any congestion-related packet drops are localized and predictable, greatly simplifying root-cause analysis when issues arise. Key 7800 architecture merits include: Deep buffer memory absorbs congestion bursts to ensure lossless AI transport Packet Loss Control to avoid packet loss Hierarchical packet buffering at DCI / WAN boundaries can enable multi-vendor XPU deployment AI Spines have Arrived The 7800 AI Spine is the nucleus connecting many distributed topologies and clusters. In a short time, Arista has designed a rich portfolio of 20+ Etherlink switches that enable 400G/800G/1.6Tbps speeds for AI use cases. Arista realizes its responsibility to enable an open AI ecosystem interoperable with leading companies such as AMD, Anthropic, Arm, Broadcom, Nvidia, OpenAI, Pure Storage and Vast Data. AI Networking requires a modern AI spine and a software stack capable of supporting foundational training and inference models that process tokens at teraflop‑scale across terabit‑class fabrics. Welcome to the new era of AI Spines and AI Centers! References: 7800R4 AI Innovators Video AI Networking White Paper

title: Start an Arizona LLC: Your Easy Step-by-Step Guide
summary: Learn how to start an Arizona LLC, including costs, steps, and benefits. Get expert help from LegalZoom with plans starting at $0 plus state filing fees.
body_text: Cost to start an LLC in Arizona All things considered, you’ll pay at least $50 for Arizona LLC registration . However, the total cost of creating an LLC in Arizona can increase to $1,000 or more, especially if you need specialized permits. Immediate formation costs Filing fee (articles of organization): $50 ($85 for expedited processing) Statutory agent: $0 to $300, depending on whether you use professional services Name reservation (optional): $10 ($45 for expedited processing) Publication costs: $30 to $300, depending on the newspaper (note that this isn’t required in Maricopa and Pima counties) Additional costs Business licenses and permits: Varies—for example, the statewide Transaction Privilege Tax (TPT) license costs $12, whereas a mobile food vending permit in Phoenix costs $350 Business insurance: $70 to $100 per month, depending on business needs and coverage type(s) Filing a trade name (DBA): $10 ($45 for expedited online filing) Certified copies of documents: $10 to $15, depending on the requested documents You might also pay fees for any corrections or revisions you submit to the ACC, so be sure to check the schedule of fees for an accurate estimate. Maintaining your LLC in Arizona Maintaining an LLC in Arizona is a little bit easier than many other states. Here’s what to be aware of. Making changes and amendments Unlike many states, Arizona doesn’t have annual LLC filing fees or reporting requirements. However, if you make updates to your business, such as changing the name, you must file an amendment with the Arizona Corporation Commission . It’s good practice to regularly review and update your LLC’s information with the ACC as needed. In the event you need to change statutory agents, you’ll need to submit a statement of change for $5 (or $40 for expedited processing). Remember: your LLC must maintain a statutory agent in Arizona at all times. Business licenses and permits Arizona doesn’t require a general state business license. However, certain types of businesses may need Arizona business licenses , including the following: LLCs selling certain products or services in Arizona may need to apply for a Transaction Privilege Tax (TPT) license, which is a tax on the business for certain types of transactions. Food service businesses need health permits for both the facility and the food handlers. Businesses that sell liquor need a license from the Arizona Department of Liquor License and Control, as well as local licenses. Child care businesses need a license from the Arizona Department of Health Services. Many cities and counties also require local licenses. For instance: Maricopa County (which includes Phoenix, Mesa, Scottsdale, and Tempe) requires food trucks, restaurants, caterers, and businesses dealing with water or air quality to have a license from the Maricopa Environmental Department . Pima County (which includes Tucson and Marana) requires food and beverage businesses, tattoo shops, and daycare facilities to have a license from the Pima Health Department . The city of Prescott requires a Peddler/Solicitor License for those making sales door-to-door. You can check with the Arizona Commerce Authority to identify the exact state or local licenses you’ll need. If you’d like assistance, LegalZoom can look into all these licenses and permits for you and identify which ones your business needs to operate. Taxes As pass-through entities, LLC members typically report income taxes on their personal returns—unless they elect to be taxed as a corporation. However, if you sell goods or services subject to the Transaction Privilege Tax, you’ll need to pay those taxes through AZTaxes.gov . If you have or plan on hiring employees, you’ll need to register with AZTaxes.gov using your EIN to set up employment tax withholding. Additionally, you must register with the Arizona Department of Economic Security (DES) for unemployment insurance tax. It’s often smart to consult a professional for legal or tax advice.

title: Tax Season Is Coming. Your Reconciliation Backlog Isn't Ready.
summary: Tax season exposes reconciliation gaps ecommerce finance teams can't afford. Learn how automated order-to-cash reconciliation across Shopify, Stripe, and NetSuite keeps your books audit-ready year-round.
body_text: Why April 15th is really a data infrastructure story for ecommerce finance teams April arrives like clockwork. And every year, finance teams at ecommerce and retail brands face the same uncomfortable truth: the chaos of tax season wasn't created in April. It was created in February, November, August — every month that reconciliation was left to pile up, every payout that went unmatched, every return that fell through the cracks between Shopify and NetSuite. Tax season doesn't cause the problem. It just makes it impossible to ignore. The Ecommerce Reconciliation Problem Is Unique Most general-purpose accounting tools weren't built for the complexity of modern commerce. A DTC brand running Shopify with Stripe, PayPal, Afterpay, and Amazon as channels, plus Loop Returns for returns management and NetSuite as its ERP, isn't dealing with a simple revenue stream. It's dealing with dozens of overlapping data sources, each with their own payout schedules, fee structures, dispute timelines, and remittance logic. When April hits, your accountant isn't just filing a return. They're trying to reconcile what Stripe paid out last quarter against what Shopify says was sold, net of returns that Loop processed, with fees that hit at different times and bank deposits that don't map cleanly to any individual order. All of it needs to agree before it goes anywhere near a tax filing. If your team is doing any part of that manually — in spreadsheets, with exports, through endless back-and-forth between platforms — you already know the cost. Not just in hours, but in confidence. Do you actually trust the revenue number you're filing? The Real Problem: Reactive Finance Most ecommerce finance teams operate reactively. Month-end close happens after the month. Reconciliation happens after the discrepancy is discovered. Tax prep happens after the year is over. The result is a consistent pattern: the bigger the brand grows, the more volume it processes, the worse the reconciliation problem becomes. Going from $20M to $200M in GMV doesn't just mean more orders, it means exponentially more complexity. More channels. More processors. More edge cases. More partial refunds, Shop Cash transactions, Global-e cross-border orders, and disputed chargebacks that none of your systems agree on. By the time April comes around, your team isn't closing books. They're archaeology. What Audit-Ready Actually Looks Like The brands that move through tax season calmly have one thing in common: their books are closing daily, not monthly. They're not scrambling to reconstruct Q4 because Q4 was already reconciled, order by order, payment by payment, payout by payout, before December 31st. That means: Every transaction has a paper trail. From the original Shopify order, through the payment processor, to the bank deposit. No gaps. No "we think this matched." Returns are fully accounted for. Loop Returns and Happy Returns are reconciled in context, the refund to the customer, the reversal from the processor, the credit memo in the ERP all agree on the same amount. Journal entries are automated. Summarized entries push into NetSuite or QuickBooks daily, not in a manual bulk upload at month-end. Your ERP reflects reality, not a lagging approximation of it. Fees are separated cleanly. Stripe's processing fees, PayPal's takes, Adyen's transaction costs, these are categorized and reconciled as part of the payout workflow, not reverse-engineered afterward. When your data layer looks like this, tax season is just another deadline. Not a fire drill. Use This April as a Forcing Function If your team is stressed right now, pay attention to where the stress is coming from. That's your roadmap. Is it that no one can explain the gap between gross Shopify sales and net bank deposits? That's a payout reconciliation problem. Is it that returns from Q4 are still floating unreconciled? That's a returns management integration problem. Is it that journal entries are being created by hand for hundreds of thousands of orders? That's a subledger problem. Every one of those pain points has a direct cost — in accountant hours, in audit exposure, in the confidence your CFO or board has in your numbers. And every one of them is solvable before next April. The question isn't whether your books get closed. The question is whether you want to close them the hard way or the right way. The Standard Is 99% Accuracy, Every Day Ecommerce finance teams shouldn't have to settle for "close enough." The margin for error in a high-volume DTC brand is too thin — chargebacks, foreign exchange, multi-currency payouts, and marketplace fee structures leave no room for manual guesswork. The standard for modern ecommerce finance is 99%+ reconciliation accuracy, maintained continuously, not recovered at quarter-end. That's not aspirational. It's achievable, when your order systems, payment processors, bank accounts, and ERP are speaking the same language through a purpose-built reconciliation layer. Tax season should be the easiest week of your quarter. If it's not, that's a signal worth taking seriously. Interested in learning more? Request a demo.

title: What It Actually Costs to Make An Empty Room Sell
summary: Virtual staging cost runs about $1–$50 per photo versus a $1,500+ median for physical staging. See what drives the price and how to stage at scale.
body_text: An Empty Room Is a Silent Price Cut An empty room like this is a silent price cut; virtual staging fixes it. A vacant living room photographs as a cold rectangle. A buyer scrolling listings on a phone can't picture a life in it, so they swipe past. You already know staging fixes that. What stops most agents is the sticker on physical staging: a median of $1,500 for a staging service , per the National Association of Realtors, before monthly furniture rental resets the meter. Virtual staging promises the same visual payoff for a sliver of that. So the question every listing agent asks is simple: what does virtual staging cost, and is the cheap version any good? What virtual staging costs in 2026 83% of buyers' agents say staging makes a home easier to picture. Virtual staging runs on two tracks, and the price gap between them is wide. AI tools sit at the bottom. Platforms like Virtual Staging AI furnish a photo for roughly a dollar; its standard plan works out to $0.95 per photo , and even the entry tier stays under $3. You upload an empty room, pick a style, and get furniture dropped in within minutes. Human-edited services sit a rung up. HomeLight pegs professional per-photo staging at $20 to $50 each . BoxBrownie, one of the larger editing shops, charges a flat $30 per image with a 48-hour turnaround and no subscription. A real editor places and scales the furniture, so shadows, reflections, and proportions hold up under a close look. Now the contrast that matters. Physical staging carries that $1,500 median for a staging service, and that covers only the first stretch; additional months of furniture rental run $150 to more than $1,000 . Furnishing six rooms virtually might cost about $180 with a $30-per-image editor , or under $20 with an AI tool . Why the price swings so much Same phrase, very different products. Four things move the number: the method (AI generation versus a human editor), the turnaround (minutes versus 24 to 48 hours), the revision policy (some services bundle changes, others bill for them), and the room count, since you pay per image and a whole-home listing adds up fast. The cheapest AI output can give itself away: floating couches, furniture that ignores the room's scale, rugs that bend where the floor doesn't. Human-edited staging costs more because someone measures the space and matches the light. On a high-end listing, that difference reads instantly to a buyer. On a quick rental turn, AI is often plenty. Our dos and don'ts of virtual staging walks through where each one fits. Is virtual staging worth the cost? The data says staging earns back its small price. In NAR's 2025 Profile of Home Staging, 29% of agents reported that staging produced a 1% to 10% increase in the dollar value offered, and 49% of sellers' agents saw staged homes spend less time on the market. Most tellingly, 83% of buyers' agents said staging made it easier for a buyer to picture the property as a future home. Photos are where that first impression forms. The same report found buyers' agents rate listing photos as highly important to 73% of their clients , and 31% of buyers were more willing to walk through a home they had seen online when it was staged to their taste. Empty rooms forfeit that moment. As we cover in our piece on why professional listing photos help homes sell faster , the image is the storefront. The real cost shows up at scale For a single listing, virtual staging is a rounding error. For a brokerage or a property management team running dozens of listings a month, the math changes. Per-photo fees multiply, turnaround times stack up, and quality drifts when every agent reaches for a different tool. One listing gets tasteful furniture scaled to the room; the next gets AI furniture sinking into the floor. That inconsistency is the cost nobody budgets for. Doing it piecemeal is what breaks down. Snappr's editing and AI staging pair AI speed with human quality control, so a 40-listing month comes back in one consistent style, on one timeline, at a predictable per-image rate. Guidelines get set once and applied to every image, and staging becomes one automated step instead of a scramble across markets. We break down the operational side in our guide to automating property photos and virtual tours . Empty rooms don't have to cost you a sale or a season on the market. Book time with Snappr's Enterprise team to see how virtual staging and editing scale across your whole portfolio. Frequently asked questions How much does virtual staging cost per photo? AI virtual staging costs roughly $1 to $3 per photo , while human-edited services generally run $20 to $50 per image . Flat-rate editors such as BoxBrownie charge about $30 per image with no subscription. Physical staging, by comparison, carries a median cost of $1,500 for a staging service . Is virtual staging cheaper than traditional staging? Yes, and by a wide margin. Furnishing a full listing virtually usually costs tens of dollars, versus a $1,500 median plus ongoing monthly rental for physical staging, according to NAR. The tradeoff is that virtual furniture lives only in the photos, not in the home during in-person showings. Does cheaper AI virtual staging look fake? It can. Low-cost AI tools sometimes produce furniture that ignores scale, lighting, or perspective. Human-edited or human-reviewed staging costs more because an editor matches proportions and light, which matters most on higher-value listings. Do you have to disclose virtual staging? Most industry guidance and many MLS rules call for disclosing that listing photos were virtually staged. It is a transparency issue: the goal is to help buyers see the potential of a space, not to misrepresent it. Label staged images clearly. Sources 1. NAR 2025 Profile of Home Staging (newsroom release) — median staging service cost, price and time-on-market impact, buyer visualization stats 2. BoxBrownie Virtual Staging — $30 per image flat human-edited virtual staging pricing 3. Virtual Staging AI Pricing — AI virtual staging plans at roughly $0.95 to $2.67 per photo 4. HomeLight: Staging vs Virtual Staging — per-photo human staging range and monthly physical staging rental costs

title: Claude Agent SDK Integrations: A Developer's Guide to Extending Agents with Custom Tools
summary: A developer's guide to Claude Agent SDK integrations, how to wire in custom tools like Jira, Slack, and Google Drive without turning each one into a maintenance project.
body_text: Building on the Claude Agent SDK gets you a solid agent loop out of the box but the moment your agent needs to touch Jira, Slack, Google Drive, or your own internal APIs, you're back to the same question every framework eventually asks: how do custom tools actually get wired in, safely, without turning into a maintenance project of their own? What "Claude Agent SDK integrations" actually means When developers search for Claude Agent SDK integrations or ask how to integrate Jira with Claude Agent SDK , they're usually trying to solve one of two problems: Exposing an existing API as a tool the agent can call mid-conversation Jira issues, Shopify orders, Mixpanel events. Wiring in a data source the agent needs to read from continuously, like Google Drive documents or a Discord channel's history. Both come down to the same underlying pattern: a typed tool definition (name, input schema, output shape) registered with the agent, plus whatever credential and rate-limit handling that tool needs behind the scenes. The SDK gives you the mechanism to register a tool. It doesn't give you the Jira client, the OAuth flow, or the retry logic that's the part teams underestimate. Tool calling frameworks vs. hand-rolled tool definitions There's a real difference between defining tools one-off, inline in your agent code, and using a proper tool calling framework . Hand-rolled tools work fine for a demo with two or three integrations. They start to strain once you have: More than a handful of tools , each with its own auth pattern, rate limits, and error handling copy-pasted with small variations. Multiple agents or environments that need the same tools, where duplicated tool definitions drift out of sync. A need for consistent logging agent tool call logging — so you can debug why an agent made a particular call, with what arguments, and what came back, across every integration uniformly. A tool calling framework centralizes this: one registration pattern, one logging format, one place credential and retry logic lives, regardless of how many tools or agents you're running. Coding agent integration: a special case worth calling out Coding agent integration — wiring an agent into CI/CD pipelines, a Git host, or a ticketing system to actually ship code changes deserves extra care beyond typical tool calling. The actions here (merging a PR, deploying to production, closing a ticket) are higher-stakes than reading a Slack message. Two practices matter more here than elsewhere: Explicit approval gates on anything that changes production state — an agent proposing a PR is very different from an agent merging one. Full audit logging per tool call , since "what did the coding agent actually do, and why" is the first question anyone asks after an incident. API key management for multi-integration agents As the number of tools grows, API key management stops being "an env variable per service" and becomes an actual operational concern: Rotation. Keys that don't get rotated regularly are a standing risk; a good integration layer supports rotating a credential without redeploying every service that uses it. Scoping. A key with full account access for a tool that only needs read permissions is unnecessary exposure request the narrowest scope the tool actually needs. Isolation per environment. Dev, staging, and production should never share the same third-party credentials, so a leaked staging key can't touch real customer data. Building custom tools without reinventing the plumbing For teams that need a tool the framework doesn't ship, a custom plugin generator pattern scaffolding a new tool with the same typed shape, auth handling, and logging as every built-in one keeps custom integrations from becoming second-class citizens in your codebase. The goal is that a tool you wrote yourself last week behaves identically, from the agent's perspective and from your logging dashboard's perspective, to one that shipped with the SDK. How Corsair extends the Claude Agent SDK Corsair plugs directly into Claude Agent SDK workflows as a typed tool layer: Jira, Slack, Google Drive, GitHub, Shopify, Mixpanel, and more are available as pre-built plugins with OAuth, rate limiting, and retry logic already handled, so you're not hand-rolling each one. Every tool call built-in plugin or custom flows through the same permission system and logging format, so agent tool call logging is consistent across your entire integration surface. Need something Corsair doesn't ship yet? Scaffold a new plugin with the same typed interface as every other one, so it's never a second-class integration in your stack. Self-host the whole thing for free with npm install corsair, or connect via a single MCP URL if you'd rather not manage the infrastructure. Whether you're building your first Claude agent or scaling a production AI workflow with dozens of integrations, Corsair removes the repetitive infrastructure work behind tool calling. Instead of maintaining custom connectors, you can focus on building better agents with a unified integration layer. Explore everything Corsair offers, from pre-built plugins to self-hosted deployment, on the Corsair homepage . See Claude Agent SDK integration examples → corsair.dev

title: Is a Fragrance Subscription Worth It? An Honest Cost Breakdown for 2026
summary: Is a fragrance subscription worth it? An honest cost breakdown for 2026, who it suits, who is better off buying bottles, and how the math compares to a $150 bottle.
body_text: Not too long ago, we covered what makes a great fragrance subscription , concluding that factors such as personalization, flexibility, and affordability should be considered. Consumers, after all, are more discerning than ever. So, is a perfume subscription actually worth it? The short answer is yes, but it might not be the same for everyone. In this piece, we’ll talk about whether a fragrance subscription makes sense for you, cost-wise. If you love experimenting with different scent families and building a fragrance wardrobe, a subscription can offer exceptional value. That said, even dedicated signature scent wearers can benefit from a fragrance subscription. It’s one of the easiest ways to discover your next favorite perfume should your tastes evolve or if you simply decide you’re ready for something different. So, Is a Perfume Subscription Worth It? For most scent enthusiasts, a fragrance subscription is worth it. A subscription isn’t simply about spending less. It’s about discovering more.
