title: UL 94-Klassifizierung und flammhemmende Materialien
summary: Eine detaillierte Analyse von thermoplastischen Werkstoffen mit flammhemmenden Eigenschaften sowie der UL-94-Klassifizierung.
body_text: Wenn Sie mit Kunststoff konstruieren und die Brandschutzklassen nicht berücksichtigt haben, riskieren Sie mehr als nur die Einhaltung der Vorschriften. UL 94 ist nicht nur ein Label. Es ist ein Türwächter. Der Unterschied zwischen einer V-0- und einer V-2-Klassifizierung kann den Unterschied zwischen einer genehmigten Produktion und einer kostspieligen Neukonstruktion ausmachen. Wenn Sie zum Beispiel schon einmal erlebt haben, dass ein technisch einwandfreies Bauteil die Zertifizierung nicht bestanden hat, weil die Wandstärke unter den Prüfgrenzwert gefallen ist, sind Sie nicht allein. Anwendungsbereiche für flammhemmende Kunststoffe Materialien mit UL 94-Zulassung werden häufig verwendet in: Komponenten im Motorraum von Kraftfahrzeugen (PA, PPS) Lüfter und Halterungen (PBT, LCP) Elektrische Gehäuse und Schaltergehäuse (PC, ABS/PC-Mischungen) Industrielle Kabelführungen und elektronische Bauteile (PP, PEEK) Gehäuse für medizinische Geräte (PPSU) Telekommunikationshardware und Steckergehäuse (ABS, PC/ABS) Diese Teile sind häufig erhöhten Temperaturen, mechanischer Belastung und der Nähe zu elektrischem Strom ausgesetzt, weshalb die Flammwidrigkeit für die Sicherheit und die Einhaltung von Vorschriften entscheidend ist. Was ist UL 94? Lassen Sie uns einmal genauer betrachten, was UL 94 eigentlich ist, warum es wichtiger ist, als den meisten Menschen bewusst ist, und wie man von Anfang an fundiertere Materialentscheidungen treffen kann. UL 94 ist eine von Underwriters Laboratories entwickelte Norm zur Entflammbarkeit von Kunststoffen. Sie bewertet, wie Kunststoffe auf offene Flamme reagieren, indem sie die Entzündungszeit, das Selbstlöschverhalten und die Frage misst, ob brennende Tropfen einen sekundären Baumwollindikator entzünden. UL 94 ist mit anderen internationalen Normen kompatibel, was ihm weltweite Relevanz für Brandschutzprüfungen verleiht. Die Prüfaufbauten variieren. Die HB-Einstufung umfasst eine horizontale Brandbewertung. Andere Einstufungsklassen – wie die V- und 5V-Serien – verwenden vertikale Stäbe oder Platten. Innerhalb der V-Serie besteht der Unterschied zwischen V-0 und V-1 darin, dass ein V-0-Material unter denselben Testbedingungen strengere Kriterien erfüllt. Die Testbedingungen werden beim Übergang von der V- zur 5V-Bewertungsgruppe strenger, wobei 5V-Tests ein höheres Maß an Entflammbarkeitsbeständigkeit erfordern. UL 94-Klassifizierungen auf einen Blick Bewertung Hauptkriterien HB Langsames Abbrennen an einer horizontalen Stelle V-2 Das Brennen hört innerhalb von 30 Sekunden auf, sodass vertikal fallende brennbare Kunststoffteile nicht mehr entzünden können V-1 An senkrechten Stellen erlischt die Flamme innerhalb von 30 Sekunden, sodass herabtropfender Kunststoff nicht mehr entflammbar ist V-0 An senkrechten Stellen erlischt die Flamme innerhalb von 10 Sekunden, sodass herabtropfender Kunststoff nicht mehr entflammbar ist 5VB Das Brennen hört an einer senkrechten Stelle innerhalb von 60 Sekunden auf, sodass keine nicht brennenden Kunststofftropfen entstehen. Die Prüfkörper dürfen durchbrennen (es darf ein Loch vorhanden sein). 5VA Wie bei 5VB, jedoch darf die Platte nicht durchbrennen. Dies ist die höchste Einstufung gemäß UL 94. Das Brennen muss bei einem senkrecht stehenden Teil innerhalb von 60 Sekunden aufhören, wobei keine nicht brennenden Kunststofftropfen zulässig sind. Die Prüfkörper dürfen keine Durchbrennstellen (keine Löcher) aufweisen. Die Einstufung von Materialien als 5VA oder 5VB erfolgt anhand eines vertikalen 125-mm-Brenntests unter Verwendung einer Bunsenbrennerflamme. Stäbe und Platten müssen bestimmte Anforderungen an Größe und Dicke erfüllen, und die Flamme wird in Intervallen von fünf Sekunden angewendet, wobei zwischen jeder Anwendung eine fünfsekündige flammenfreie Pause eingelegt wird. Bei der V-Serie wird eine 20-mm-Flamme zweimal für jeweils zehn Sekunden angewendet. Die zweite Flamme wird angewendet, sobald die Probe nicht mehr brennt, oder sofort, falls sie gar nicht erst Feuer fängt. UL 94-Prüfkonfigurationen Horizontaler Brandtest 20-mm-Vertikalbrandtest 125-mm-Vertikalbrandtest (bar) 125 mm vertikaler Brand (Plakette) Flammhemmend vs. flammfest: Was ist der Unterschied? Flammhemmende Materialien sind so konzipiert, dass sie die Entzündung verzögern und die Flammenausbreitung unterdrücken. Sie können zwar Feuer fangen, erlöschen jedoch von selbst, sobald die Zündquelle entfernt wird. Die Klassifizierungen nach UL 94 fallen in diese Kategorie. Flammbeständige Materialien hingegen widerstehen der Entzündung vollständig und werden häufig in Textilien oder persönlicher Schutzausrüstung verwendet. Diese werden nach anderen Normen geprüft, wie beispielsweise ASTM D6413 oder ISO 15025. Das Verständnis dieses Unterschieds hilft Ingenieuren dabei, Materialien sowohl nach ihrer funktionalen Leistung als auch nach ihrer Konformität mit den Vorschriften auszuwählen. Warum Dicke und Rezeptur entscheidend sind Die Einstufungen nach UL 94 sind dickeabhängig. Ein Kunststoff, der bei einer Dicke von 0,059 Zoll (1,5 mm) die Anforderungen erfüllt, kann bei einer Dicke von 0,029 Zoll (0,74 mm) durchfallen. Manche Materialien weisen über einen weiten Bereich von Wandstärken hinweg ein gleichbleibendes Verhalten auf, dies ist jedoch nicht garantiert. Auch die Zusammensetzung spielt eine entscheidende Rolle. Die meisten flammhemmenden Typen sind auf bestimmte Additive angewiesen, um die Leistungsziele zu erreichen. Selbst kleine Änderungen (wie der Wechsel von Farbstoffen) können die Zertifizierung ungültig machen, es sei denn, die neue Mischung wird unabhängig getestet und zertifiziert. Fragen Sie im Zweifelsfall Ihren Materiallieferanten nach einer UL Yellow Card – einer Bescheinigung, dass das Material Sicherheits- und Leistungstests durchlaufen hat. Diese sollte die vollständige Zusammensetzung und Ihren erforderlichen Dickenbereich abdecken. Flammhemmende Materialien bei Protolabs erhältlich Wir bieten eine Vielzahl von Materialien mit UL-94-Zulassung für den Spritzguss und den 3D-Druck an. Auf Anfrage können auch vom Kunden bereitgestellte Kunststoffe geprüft werden. Bitte beachten Sie, dass ein und dasselbe Material je nach verschiedenen Faktoren unterschiedliche Einstufungen aufweisen kann, sodass man nicht pauschal sagen kann, dass ein Material die Einstufung V-0 hat. Zusätzlich zu den Dutzenden von Materialien mit UL 94-Zulassung für den Spritzguss haben wir zwei flammhemmende Materialien für den 3D-Druck in unser Sortiment aufgenommen: ESD Black (Loctite 3380) Dieses Harz ist nach UL 94 V-0 bei einer Dicke von 2,0 mm (0,08 Zoll) eingestuft. Es verfügt über elektrostatisch ableitende (ESD) Eigenschaften und eignet sich gut für gedruckte Teile, die eine hohe Genauigkeit und feine Details erfordern. Arkema FR512 Dieses flammhemmende Photopolymer, das in unserem HPS-Verfahren zum Einsatz kommt, erfüllt die Norm UL 94 V-0 bei einer Dicke von 0,031 Zoll (0,79 mm). Es eignet sich ideal für komplexe Teile, die eine hohe Detailgenauigkeit und zertifizierte Flammhemmung erfordern. Erfahren Sie mehr über flammhemmende Materialien für den 3D-Druck PFAS in flammhemmenden Materialien Per- und Polyfluoralkylsubstanzen (PFAS) werden aufgrund ihrer außergewöhnlichen thermischen und chemischen Beständigkeit seit langem in flammhemmenden Additiven eingesetzt. Aufgrund ihrer Langlebigkeit in der Umwelt und ihres Zusammenhangs mit potenziellen Gesundheitsrisiken stehen PFAS jedoch zunehmend unter regulatorischem Druck. Zwar enthalten einige flammhemmende Materialien nach wie vor PFAS, doch viele Hersteller verzichten zunehmend auf deren Verwendung. Wir beobachten die PFAS-Vorschriften genau. Obwohl der PFAS-Gehalt derzeit nicht in unseren Materialdaten aufgeführt ist, empfehlen wir Kunden mit regulatorischen oder ökologischen Bedenken, sich an uns zu wenden. Wir können Ihnen bei der Suche nach Alternativen helfen oder bei Bedarf spezifische Harzzusammensetzungen bestätigen. Umweltaspekte Flammschutzmittel verbessern die Brandsicherheit, können jedoch die Entsorgung von Produkten am Ende ihrer Lebensdauer erschweren. Halogenierte Additive lassen sich beim Recycling nur schwer abtrennen und können bei der Verbrennung giftige Verbindungen freisetzen. Aus diesem Grund wächst das Interesse an halogenfreien Flammschutzmitteln, die eine ähnliche Leistungsfähigkeit bei geringerer Umweltbelastung bieten. Bei der Materialauswahl sollten stets sowohl Sicherheits- als auch Nachhaltigkeitsaspekte berücksichtigt werden. Warum Brandschutzklassen in der Produktentwicklung wichtig sind Die UL 94-Klassifizierungen sind nicht nur technische Details. Sie entscheiden oft darüber, ob ein Bauteil in regulierten Branchen wie der Luft- und Raumfahrt, der Medizintechnik, der Automobilindustrie und der Unterhaltungselektronik eingesetzt werden kann. Die frühzeitige Auswahl eines zertifizierten Materials mit Brandschutzklasse hilft, Probleme bei der Einhaltung von Vorschriften, kostspielige Neukonstruktionen und fehlgeschlagene Zertifizierungen in späten Entwicklungsphasen zu vermeiden. Noch eine Sache, bevor Sie Ihren Entwurf einreichen Die UL-Zertifizierung ist formulierungsspezifisch. Ein Kunststoff kann zwar eine „Yellow Card“ tragen, doch kundenspezifische Mischungen, Farbstoffe, Additive und andere Veränderungen am Ausgangsmaterial können die Einstufung beeinflussen. Wenn Sie in Branchen tätig sind, in denen mehrere Eigenschaftsnormen gelten, wie z. B. in Bezug auf Rauchentwicklung, Toxizität oder thermische Alterung, sollten Sie vor der Produktion unbedingt das vollständige Materialprofil validieren. Weitere Informationen zu den Eigenschaften von Spritzgussmaterialien finden Sie in unserem Leitfaden zur Auswahl von Spritzgussmaterialien . UL 94 mag wie ein regulatorisches Kleingedrucktes erscheinen, spielt jedoch eine entscheidende Rolle dabei, was gebaut, was zugelassen und was zur Überarbeitung zurückgewiesen wird. Unsere Anwendungsingenieure stehen Ihnen zur Verfügung, um Ihnen zu helfen, die richtige Entscheidung für Ihre Anwendung, Ihr Budget und Ihren Zeitplan zu treffen. Angebot anfordern Sind Sie bereit, ein Material mit UL 94-Zulassung zu wählen und kostspielige Neukonstruktionen zu vermeiden? Laden Sie Ihr Bauteil hoch , um sofort Preise und Lieferzeiten zu erhalten. Häufig gestellte Fragen Was ist UL 94 und warum ist das wichtig? expand_less expand_more UL 94 ist eine Norm der Underwriters Laboratories zur Entflammbarkeit von Kunststoffen, die bewertet, wie Materialien auf offene Flammen und Zündung reagieren, wie ihr Selbstlöschverhalten ist und ob brennende Tropfen einen Baumwollindikator entzünden. Sie ist weithin anerkannt und wird in regulierten Branchen häufig vorgeschrieben; daher kann die von Ihnen gewählte Einstufung darüber entscheiden, ob ein Bauteil die Zertifizierung besteht oder neu konstruiert werden muss. Was bedeuten die wichtigsten UL-94-Klassifizierungen (HB, V und 5V)? expand_less expand_more HB: Langsames Abbrennen an einem horizontalen Prüfkörper. V-2: Der vertikale Prüfkörper erlischt innerhalb von 30 Sekunden; brennende Tropfen, die Baumwolle entzünden können, sind zulässig. V-1: Der vertikale Prüfkörper erlischt innerhalb von 30 Sekunden; keine brennenden Tropfen, die Baumwolle entzünden. V-0: Der vertikale Prüfkörper erlischt innerhalb von 10 Sekunden; keine brennenden Tropfen, die Baumwolle entzünden. 5VB/5VA: Strengere vertikale Prüfungen mit einer größeren Flamme; brennende Tropfen sind nicht zulässig. 5VB erlaubt Durchbrennen (Löcher), während 5VA, die höchste UL 94-Einstufung, dies nicht zulässt. Inwiefern beeinflussen die Materialstärke und die Zusammensetzung die Einstufung nach UL 94? expand_less expand_more Die Klassifizierungen sind dickeabhängig und formulierungsspezifisch. Ein Kunststoff, der bei einer Dicke von 1,5 mm die V-0-Klasse erfüllt, kann bei einer Dicke von 0,8 mm die Anforderungen nicht mehr erfüllen, und selbst geringfügige Änderungen an der Rezeptur (wie z. B. ein neuer Farbstoff) können eine zuvor erteilte Klassifizierung ungültig machen. Überprüfen Sie stets die UL-Yellow-Card des Materials und vergewissern Sie sich, dass diese genau Ihre Rezeptur und Ihren Dickenbereich abdeckt. Was ist der Unterschied zwischen flammhemmenden und flammbeständigen Materialien? expand_less expand_more Flammhemmende Materialien sind so konzipiert, dass sie die Entzündung verzögern und selbstverlöschen, sobald die Zündquelle entfernt wird (hier gilt UL 94). Flammfeste Materialien sind so ausgelegt, dass sie einer Entzündung gänzlich widerstehen, und werden nach anderen Normen geprüft (z. B. ASTM D6413, ISO 15025), die üblicherweise für Textilien und persönliche Schutzausrüstung (PSA) verwendet werden. Welche flammhemmenden Materialien sind bei Protolabs erhältlich, und wie sieht es mit PFAS und Umweltbedenken aus? expand_less expand_more Protolabs bietet zahlreiche nach UL 94 klassifizierte Kunststoffe für den Spritzguss sowie ausgewählte flammhemmende Optionen für den 3D-Druck an. Beispiel: Arkema FR512 (Photopolymer) erreicht die Einstufung UL 94 V-0 bei einer Dicke von 0,031 Zoll (0,79 mm). Vom Kunden bereitgestellte Kunststoffe können auf Anfrage geprüft werden. Beachten Sie, dass die Einstufungen je nach Typ und Dicke variieren; gehen Sie nicht pauschal von „V-0“ aus. Einige flammhemmende Systeme können PFAS oder halogenierte Additive enthalten; wir beobachten die Vorschriften und können Ihnen helfen, die Zusammensetzung des Kunststoffs zu bestätigen oder halogenfreie Alternativen zu prüfen, um die Recyclingfähigkeit und Umweltziele zu unterstützen.

body_text: vTv Therapeutics Announces Inducement Grants under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4) July 28, 2026 PDF Version HIGH POINT, N.C., July 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- vTv Therapeutics Inc. (Nasdaq: VTVT), a late-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the development of cadisegliatin , a novel, potential first-in-class oral adjunctive therapy to insulin being investigated for the treatment of type 1 diabetes (T1D), today announced that it granted 23,500 stock options to purchase shares of common stock to two non-executive employees as a material inducement to employment in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4). The stock options that were granted have a weighted average exercise price of $31.95 per share. Each option award will vest over a 4-year period, with 25% of the shares underlying the option vesting on the one-year anniversary of the applicable vesting commencement date and the remaining shares thereafter vesting quarterly over the following 36 months, subject to continued employment with vTv on such vesting dates. The options have a term of 10 years and are subject to the terms and conditions of the 2026 Inducement Plan and the stock option agreement covering the grant. About vTv Therapeutics vTv Therapeutics is a late-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing oral, small molecule drug candidates intended to help treat people living with diabetes and other chronic diseases. vTv’s clinical pipeline is led by cadisegliatin , currently in a US Phase 3 trial, a potential first-in-class oral glucokinase activator being investigated for the treatment of type 1 diabetes. vTv and its development partners are investigating multiple molecules across different indications for chronic diseases. Learn more at vtvtherapeutics.com or follow the company on LinkedIn or X . About Cadisegliatin Cadisegliatin (TTP399) is a novel, oral small molecule, liver-selective glucokinase activator being investigated in the US as a potential first-in-class oral adjunctive treatment for type 1 diabetes (T1D). In non-clinical studies, cadisegliatin acted selectively on the liver and increased the activity of glucokinase independently from insulin. These studies support clinical investigation of whether cadisegliatin can improve glycemic control through hepatic glucose uptake and glycogen storage. Cadisegliatin has been granted Breakthrough Therapy designation by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). Cadisegliatin is under investigation, and the safety and efficacy have not been established. There is no guarantee that this product will receive health authority approval or become commercially available for the use being investigated. title: 6 Best accounts payable software in 2026
summary: Compare the top AP automation tools for 2026. From AI-powered invoice coding to global payments, find the best fit for your finance stack based on pricing, features, and ERP integrations.
body_text: Choosing the best accounts payable software in 2026 depends on your invoice volume, approval complexity, and the accounting systems you already use. In this guide, we compare leading AP tools on features, pricing, and integrations so you can find the option that fits your finance stack and growth stage. At-a-glance comparison table Software Best for Key features (high level) Price* Ideal company size BILL Accounts Payable AI-powered AP automation at scale AI invoice coding, approval workflows, 130+ country payments, fraud detection $49/user/month [2] SMB to enterprise Ramp Free AP with spend management OCR capture, AI agents, corporate cards, per-transaction fees apply $0/user/month [8] Startups to mid-market Tipalti Global payables and mass payments 120+ currencies, supplier portal, tax compliance, FX hedging $99/month [11] Mid-market to enterprise Stampli Collaborative AP for ERP-centric teams Stampli AI, in-house ERP integrations, invoice collaboration Quote-based [14] Mid-market to enterprise Melio Simple bill pay for small businesses Bill capture, card-to-ACH, mobile app, approval workflows $0/month [17] Small businesses Yooz High-volume invoice processing Smart OCR, per-document pricing, 250+ integrations, fraud detection $1.99/document [19] SMB to enterprise *Pricing and features are based on publicly available information as of March 2026 and may change. Always confirm details with each provider. How we chose the best accounts payable software† In this list, we evaluated accounts payable tools based on: Core capabilities. Invoice capture, approval workflows, payment options, and accounting/ERP integrations. Automation and AI. The degree to which the platform reduces manual work through intelligent automation, from basic OCR to autonomous AI agents. Scalability and usability. Support for growing invoice volumes, multi-entity structures, and non-technical users. Total cost of ownership. Published pricing where available, plus transaction fees and typical implementation considerations. ‍ Fit for different business types. From small businesses to larger, multi-entity organizations with global payment needs. Our top picks for 2026 {{listicle-ap}} Key questions about accounts payable software What is accounts payable software? Accounts payable software automates the process of receiving, reviewing, approving, and paying vendor invoices. Instead of managing invoices through email, spreadsheets, and manual data entry, AP software brings the entire workflow into a single platform—from the moment an invoice arrives to the point where payment is sent and recorded in your accounting system. Modern AP platforms go beyond basic digitization. They use AI and machine learning to extract invoice data, detect duplicates, route approvals automatically, and flag potential fraud—reducing the manual work that traditionally makes AP one of the most time-consuming functions in finance. How does accounts payable software work? Invoice capture: Vendors email or upload invoices, and the system automatically extracts key data—vendor name, amount, line items, due date—using OCR and AI. Coding and matching: The software assigns GL codes based on historical patterns and matches invoices against purchase orders and receipts (2-way or 3-way matching). Approval routing: Invoices are routed to the right approvers based on configurable rules such as amount, department, vendor, or project. Payment execution: Approved invoices are grouped into payment runs via ACH, check, card, wire, or international transfer. Sync and reconciliation: Transactions sync back to the general ledger or ERP, giving finance teams real-time visibility into cash outflows and outstanding liabilities. What features should you look for in accounts payable software? Invoice processing automation: AI-powered data extraction, duplicate detection, and automatic GL coding to reduce manual entry. Approval workflows: Multi-level routing based on amount, department, or vendor, with mobile approvals and audit trails. Payment options: ACH, checks, cards, wires, and international/multi-currency support to match how your vendors want to be paid. PO matching: Automated 2-way and 3-way matching to catch discrepancies before payment. Integration capabilities: Native two-way sync with your accounting software or ERP—QuickBooks, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Xero, or Microsoft Dynamics. Fraud detection: Real-time monitoring and predictive analysis to catch suspicious invoices and payment anomalies. How much does accounts payable software cost? AP software pricing varies by vendor and model: Per-user subscriptions range from $0 (Ramp's free tier [8]) to $89/user/month (BILL's Corporate plan [2]). BILL starts at $49/user/month with transaction fees applied separately. [2] Flat monthly plans with unlimited users are available from Tipalti, starting at $99/month. [11] Per-document pricing is available from Yooz, starting at $1.99 per document for lower volumes and scaling down to $1.00 at high volumes. [19] Quote-based pricing is used by Stampli [14] and for enterprise tiers across most platforms. Transaction fees are common and vary by payment method [2]. Benefits of accounts payable software AP automation delivers measurable improvements across several areas: Faster processing and fewer errors. AI-powered invoice capture and coding eliminate manual data entry, reducing processing time by 20% or more and improving accuracy on key fields to 99%. [1][3] Automated matching catches duplicate invoices and discrepancies before payment. Stronger fraud prevention. Modern AP platforms use predictive AI to monitor transactions in real-time, flagging suspicious activity such as unexpected vendor banking changes or duplicate payment attempts. BILL, for example, processes 5M+ fraud predictions daily across its network. [1] Better cash flow visibility. Real-time dashboards and automated sync with accounting software give finance teams a live view of outstanding liabilities, upcoming payments, and available cash—supporting more accurate forecasting and faster month-end close. Reduced cost per invoice. By automating capture, coding, approval, and payment, AP software replaces manual steps that traditionally require printing, routing, data entry, and filing—significantly reducing the total cost to process each invoice. How to choose the right accounts payable software for your business Factor How it affects your decision Invoice volume High-volume operations benefit from AI-powered automation and per-document pricing. Lower volumes may be well-served by simpler tools with lower monthly costs. International payments If you pay vendors in multiple countries and currencies, prioritize platforms with built-in global payment support and tax compliance. ERP and accounting system Match the platform to your accounting software. Check whether integrations are native two-way sync or manual export—and whether they're included in your pricing tier. Team size and roles Compare per-user vs. per-document vs. flat-rate pricing. Consider whether approver-only users, requestors, or admins are charged separately. Approval complexity Multi-level, department-based, or amount-based routing requires configurable approval workflows. Simpler operations may only need basic authorization. Growth plans If you expect to add entities, locations, or international vendors, choose a platform that supports multi-entity management and global payments without requiring a migration. title: How Gracent Cut Administrative Headcount Requirements by 50% with Kaizen
summary: Discover how this pediatric therapy provider eliminated manual eligibility verification workflows and reclaimed bandwidth for more patient-facing work with Kaizen.
body_text: 50% reduction in administrative headcount requirements 90% of eligibility verification workflows automated by Kaizen $9.6K in revenue recovered monthly by eliminating session write-offs "With Kaizen, it feels like we have an entire digital workforce at our disposal. In fact, we would have needed to double our current headcount to get through the same amount of work. It's been an absolute gamechanger." - Kristi Hamilton, Revenue Cycle Director at Gracent About Gracent is a leading pediatric therapy provider offering ABA therapy, neuropsychology, and developmental support to children with autism across the United States. Backed by Altamont Capital and KKR, the organization supports families through established brands like North Shore Pediatric Therapy and Gracent Pediatric Therapy, with 17 locations across Illinois and Texas. Challenge Resource-intensive authorizations drained bandwidth for patient-facing work Like many organizations operating in the fast-moving and heavily regulated healthcare vertical, Gracent is no stranger to the administrative overhead associated with prior authorizations. However, as they scaled, increasing both locations and patient count, this once-manageable task quickly became an all-consuming bottleneck. Kristi Hamilton , Revenue Cycle Director at Gracent, witnessed this challenge firsthand. With 15+ patients onboarded every day for neuropsych alone, her lean team would spend countless hours verifying benefits, submitting authorizations into their EMR, and handling PDFs for documentation. Not only did these tedious, manual processes leave little to no bandwidth for patient-facing work, but they also caused authorization delays that directly impacted bottom-line revenue. "We would receive messages that patients were coming in within an hour, and we still didn't have verification completed," Kristi shares. "If we couldn't get their information in time, we would simply have to write that session off." Kristi knew that adding internal headcount or migrating to an EMR that didn't require manual authorization for every patient would be highly complex, expensive, and time-consuming. So, she sought a solution that would empower her lean team to place their most repetitive tasks on autopilot through comprehensive, flexible, and no-code automations. Fortunately, she didn't have to search for long. After consulting with trusted colleagues within the industry, Gracent's CFO recommended Kaizen , and Kristi immediately knew its healthcare-tailored workflows would be the ideal fit. "We had an authorization team of five people, each dedicated to a specific area of treatment, and everybody was busy from the minute they clocked in to the minute they clocked out. Nobody wants to be bogged down in work like that. That's why we use Kaizen." Solution A digital employee that streamlines core workflows in minutes Getting started with Kaizen was a quick and collaborative process. Kristi worked directly with the Kaizen team to build immediate familiarity and decode complex programming logic in a way that felt accessible and intuitive. "Their team's continuous assistance made us feel incredibly supported," Kristi shares. "They were always willing to get on a call, walk through the logic of our workflows, and ensure we were extracting maximum value from the partnership." Today, Gracent executes all authorization workflows spanning applied behavior analysis, occupational therapy, physical therapy, speech therapy, and neuropsych testing through Kaizen. Each authorization workflow runs autonomously, triggering follow-up actions based on previous results without human intervention. For Kristi, Kaizen has impacted her team in the following ways: Automated eligibility verification Kaizen now handles 50-90% of all eligibility verification workflows at Gracent, pulling verification needs, submitting data to external systems, generating a clean PDF, and automatically classifying documents within the organization's records. This alone has saved Kristi's team countless hours per week, which they now allocate to more proactive, patient-facing work. Seamless system integration Because Kaizen integrates with Gracent's VOB system, it eliminates manual submissions, status checks, and messy document exports. Now, Kristi's team automatically generates cleaner, audit-ready PDFs and classifies them directly into the EMR without introducing any administrative overhead. Enhanced teamwide visibility At the end of every workflow, Kaizen emails a condensed summary to all team members detailing which clients were engaged, the outcome of the interaction, and whether they experienced anything out of the ordinary. These emails not only eliminate knowledge silos but also help the team prioritize automations that might need slight tweaks to better meet client standards. Proactive reporting capabilities Kaizen's impact extends far beyond operational workflows, serving as a critical layer of oversight for Gracent's leadership. When changes in Illinois law introduced new supervision requirements for clinicians, Gracent's existing systems struggled in tracking the necessary data. Kristi's team utilized Kaizen to synthesize disparate information from Power BI and other internal reports, creating a real-time visibility tool that flags non-compliance by location. This automated oversight eliminates the need for manual data manipulation or expensive software add-ons, providing Gracent, and its stakeholders, with a scalable framework to maintain clinical standards during rapid expansion. For Gracent, a fast-moving pediatric therapy provider with a lean administrative team, Kaizen proved to be the ultimate unlock. "Kaizen enables us to focus on the real work of helping families and providing transformative care. I'm just waiting for it to one day say, 'Good morning, Kristi, what do you want me to do today?' because it's so advanced." Results Effortless authorization flows, reclaimed revenue, and a foundation for further efficiency With Kaizen, Gracent unlocked a fundamentally new approach to healthcare administration, automating up to 90% of authorizations while transitioning from reactive data entry to proactive patient care. 50% reduction in administrative headcount requirements 90% of eligibility verification workflows automated by Kaizen $9.6K in revenue recovered monthly by eliminating session write-offs Looking ahead, Gracent plans to scale these efficiencies into patient accounts and credentialing while exploring chained workflows and automated reporting to support the organization's continued growth. "My team talks every week about opportunities for automation and what we can do with Kaizen. We know the more that Kaizen grows and updates on their end, the more efficiency gains we'll unlock."

title: 5 Key Benefits of Using a Data Fabric
summary: The benefits of a data fabric span from accelerating the speed of app development to driving digital innovation.
body_text: Key data fabric benefits. As with any new innovation, the data fabric you choose must prove to be value added for the business in order to garner your organization’s investment. Let’s take a look at some of the real-world benefits of data fabrics. 1. Simplified system integrations. Data fabrics provide a single point of access to all data sources. With a data fabric architecture, you do not need to hook into system-to-system API calls directly in order to access data—the APIs are abstracted away. This abstraction lets you take advantage of the data in different systems without needing to know what the source system is or how to connect to it. Data fabric takes a unique approach to integrating data sources by keeping them where they are and creating a virtualized data layer in a centralized platform, complete with the ability to connect, relate, and extend data. This completely eliminates costly, time-consuming, and error-prone custom integration projects and greatly reduces maintenance over time. 2. Faster time to market for applications. Because data fabrics take away some of the burden of managing data in applications by stitching together your data sources, the data integration process is streamlined. With a streamlined integration process, it’s faster and easier to develop new applications that require access to multiple data sources. Projects that once stalled or even failed to get off the ground due to data management issues are now brought to life weeks and months earlier. 3. Better business insights with a complete view of your data. Data fabrics provide a comprehensive view of data, giving you a single source of truth across the enterprise. With data fabric design, you can take data from the cloud, on-premises, and multiple sources and formats and drive it into a single location. This data management architecture also provides real-time insights with a virtual data layer that updates the source data across disparate systems as you make changes across the applications that use it. The complete and accurate 360-degree view of data this approach provides helps business leaders make better decisions. With data fabrics, businesses gain insights into customer behavior, market trends, and operational performance, enabling data-driven decisions that lead to better outcomes. 4. Improved data governance. Because data fabrics keep all your data in one virtualized data model, you get a full, unified view of all your different systems. With your data in one place, you can see exactly how it is being used across the organization and take action to lock it where it doesn’t need to be exposed. This allows you to implement new modes of data access in an easy, manageable way. It’s also easy for organizations to establish clear rules for data management in a data fabric, including who can view data, who can enter data, and who can edit data. For example, using a data fabric, you can reference data in your CRM to enforce whether specific rows of data from your HR system should be accessible. You can also build custom fields, like service level agreements (SLAs), by referencing customer data and case data, even when they aren’t located in the same system. This data management approach helps you ensure compliance with regulations and enables you to better protect sensitive data with a centralized view of where and how your data is being used. 5. Faster digital innovation. Data fabric architectures provide a foundation for digital innovation by helping organizations leverage the full potential of their data. By providing a unified, consistent data view, data fabrics enable organizations to quickly develop new applications, products, and services that they wouldn’t be able to create otherwise, driving innovation and growth across each new project. Data fabrics also allow you to democratize data throughout your organization. With a data fabric, your data is no longer only accessible to people with advanced data and software development skills. Business users are able to build and manage data on their own with strict IT governance. Employees across the organization who are already familiar with the type of data they’re collecting can now use it to rapidly discover real-time strategic insights and competitive advantages. Data is the oil that fuels the digital economy. As businesses generate, collect, and store more data, they face new challenges in harnessing it effectively. Data fabrics help eliminate data silos and wrangle data into a single, unified view. And they have the flexibility, speed, and governance advantages that will benefit organizations now and into the future as the technology evolves.

title: What Makes VSee the Most-Trusted Telehealth Platform Provider?
summary: VSee telehealth powers NASA’s space station, HHS ASPR operations, and community clinics nationwide. Learn why they choose VSee as their HIPAA-compliant, no-code platform.
body_text: Why Does Architecture Matter in a Telehealth Platform? When HHS ASPR needed a telehealth system that could run national disaster response — offline, in hurricane conditions, across disconnected field sites — “secure video and patient intake” was not nearly enough. That is an extreme case but the underlying pressure is the same for any health system running hundreds of concurrent visits, multiple specialties, and complex EMR workflows: architecture is either an asset or a bottleneck. Most telehealth platforms are monolithic: they ship as a fixed product with a predetermined workflow. If your clinical process does not match the vendor’s assumptions, you are either stuck adapting your practice to the software, or you are waiting 12 to 18 months for a custom integration. VSee takes a different approach. The Building Blocks Model VSee’s platform is built on modular components we call Building Blocks — they can be assembled, configured, and reconfigured to match any clinical workflow without custom development. Need a virtual urgent care queue? That is a configuration, not a project. Need to add AI-assisted triage, an offline EMR, or remote device integrations like a stethoscope or blood pressure monitor? Those are modules you can turn on. The VSee Building Blocks platform: modular telehealth capabilities built to be fast to deploy, secure, and scalable. This architecture is why VSee clients go live in days, not months, and why organizations as operationally complex as HHS ASPR use VSee for national-scale disaster telemedicine. HIPAA Compliance Built Into the Foundation VSee does not treat HIPAA as a feature. It is the infrastructure itself: encryption at rest and in transit at the core, not layered on afterward. Video sessions are end-to-end encrypted and never routed through consumer cloud environments. Audit logging, role-based access controls, and BAAs are standard on every enterprise contract, not upsells. This is the same compliance foundation that cleared FedRAMP High review, far beyond what HIPAA alone requires. For federal and government buyers: VSee holds an HHS-issued FedRAMP High Authority to Operate (ATO). We are the only combined EHR and telehealth system to achieve this level of security. For the VA, DoD, and federal health agencies, this unparalleled compliance is often the deciding factor. Read the full FedRAMP overview here. Proven at Scale — Real Deployments, Not Demos Any vendor can show you a polished demo. What matters is what happens when the platform is under operational load, in high-stakes environments, at scale. VSee’s deployment track record includes: NASA Space Station (11+ years): Real-time telehealth platform for astronauts aboard the International Space Station. VSee is also part of the Artemis moon mission program. HHS ASPR: VSee powers the national disaster telemedicine network — deployed for the U.S. Ebola outbreak response in Kenya within 24 hours. The system includes VSee’s offline-online EMR for use in connectivity-degraded disaster environments. Qatar Ministry of Public Health: Country-wide telehealth deployment across its public hospitals These are not case study titles. They are active, ongoing contracts and deployments. No-Code Setup — What That Actually Means “No-code” is one of the most overused phrases in healthcare software. Here is what it means specifically for VSee: A healthcare organization — a hospital system, a clinic network, a government health agency that can configure and deploy a fully branded telehealth environment using VSee’s Building Blocks without writing a single line of custom code. Provider onboarding, patient intake forms, queue management, waiting room branding, device integrations, and EMR connections are all handled through configuration, not development. For context: the average custom telehealth integration project runs six to eighteen months and costs hundreds of thousands of dollars in IT labor. VSee’s no-code model eliminates that entirely for the majority of deployment scenarios. API-First — For Teams That Want to Build on Top of VSee Not every organization wants a turnkey platform. Some have developer teams and existing patient portals, EHRs, or third-party systems, and they need telehealth embedded directly into what they already have, not bolted on beside it. VSee’s API lets health IT teams integrate video visits, scheduling, patient queues, and clinical data flows directly into their own platforms. No rip-and-replace. No parallel system running alongside Epic or Oracle Health. For large health systems that have invested years and millions into their EHR environment, this is the difference between a telehealth vendor and a telehealth infrastructure layer. Offline-Online EMR — Built for Environments Others Cannot Reach One of VSee’s most distinctive technical capabilities is its offline-online EMR — a clinical records system that functions fully without internet connectivity and syncs automatically when connectivity is restored. This was not built for a theoretical use case. It was built for VSee’s work with ASPR in disaster response environments, and for projects like the Philippine Tuberculosis Society initiative, which uses VSee’s low-connectivity, AI-powered telemedicine EMR to screen TB patients in remote field settings. For organizations operating in rural health, military, occupational health, or emergency medicine contexts, this capability is rare, and often decisive. Frequently Asked Questions What is the best telehealth platform for healthcare organizations? The best telehealth platform for a healthcare organization depends on its size, regulatory environment, and workflow complexity. VSee is consistently rated among the most trusted options for enterprise and government healthcare because of its HHS-issued FedRAMP High Authority to Operate (ATO) in production for ASPR, alongside rapid, no-code configurability that lets teams adjust workflows in hours or days rather than months. This reliability is backed by more than a decade of live deployments across health systems, government agencies, and NASA. Is VSee HIPAA compliant? Yes. VSee is a HIPAA-compliant telehealth platform. Video sessions are end-to-end encrypted, data is stored on secure infrastructure with role-based access controls and audit logging, and VSee signs Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) with enterprise clients. This same security foundation supports VSee’s HHS-issued FedRAMP High ATO for government and federal health deployments. Does VSee have a FedRAMP High ATO? Yes. VSee holds a FedRAMP High Authority to Operate (ATO) issued by HHS ASPR, assessed against the full FedRAMP High control baseline. FedRAMP High is the highest FedRAMP impact level, reserved for the most sensitive federal data — which is what makes VSee suitable for the VA, DoD, and other federal health networks. What is VSee’s Building Blocks architecture? VSee’s Building Blocks are modular components that can be assembled and configured to match any clinical workflow without custom development. Instead of adapting your practice to rigid software or waiting months for a custom integration, teams turn capabilities on and configure them — which is why VSee organizations can go live in days rather than months. Can VSee integrate with EMR systems like Epic? Yes. VSee integrates with EMR and EHR systems over standard HL7 and FHIR interfaces, including Epic and Oracle Health (formerly Cerner), as well as through VSee’s own API for deeper custom integration — so telehealth fits into your existing systems without a rip-and-replace. The Bottom Line VSee is known for its simple yet robust platform, intentionally built for environments where failure is not an option. It is the platform of choice for rural disaster response, federal government healthcare, major hospital systems, and space. If your organization needs a telehealth platform that can be deployed quickly, scaled reliably, and trusted completely, VSee is worth a serious evaluation. Ready to see VSee in your environment? title: Eve Air Mobility and FDOT partner to advance advanced air mobility in Florida
summary: The effort will focus on delivering insights into infrastructure, operational procedures, and airspace navigation procedures.
body_text: Eve Air Mobility is announcing a partnership with the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) for a focused advanced air mobility (AAM) initiative at SunTrax Air. The FDOT-led initiative will bring together Eve’s expertise in eVTOL aircraft, operations, and services with SunTrax Air’s research, testing, and validation capabilities. The effort will focus on delivering insights into the infrastructure, operational procedures, and airspace navigation procedures needed to enable the safe and efficient integration of advanced air mobility into Florida’s transportation network. “Florida recognizes its strategic role in the future of advanced air mobility and is proactively building the ecosystem needed to support it,” said Johann Bordais, chief executive officer of Eve Air Mobility. “Chief Will Watts and the FDOT team understand that successfully introducing a new mode of transportation requires alignment across aircraft, infrastructure, operations, and communities. Building on Embraer’s longstanding relationship with the state, Eve is proud to bring its expertise to help advance Florida’s vision and readiness for eVTOL operations.” Owned and operated by FDOT, SunTrax Air serves as Florida’s dedicated advanced air mobility research and development hub, providing a collaborative environment to evaluate technologies, operational concepts, and supporting infrastructure for next-generation aviation. “This partnership is another step of forward-progress being made in Florida toward achieving the implementation of advanced air mobility,” said Jared W. Perdue, P.E., FDOT Secretary. “The unique resources and infrastructure found only at SunTrax will play a key role in Eve’s research and testing needed to ensure the safe integration of Advanced Air Mobility into our transportation system.” The partnership builds on the growing relationship between Eve and FDOT. Through ongoing collaboration, the organizations will work to position Florida as a national leader in AAM. Using SunTrax Air’s purpose-built research and testing environment, they will evaluate operational concepts, infrastructure readiness, passenger experience, and future ecosystem requirements, creating a foundation that supports Florida’s long-term transportation strategy while helping accelerate the commercialization of advanced air mobility. This press release was prepared and distributed by Eve Air Mobility.

title: Solving Complex Material Challenges
summary: When steel challenges get technical, Worthington Steel's CML team steps in. Learn how our experts solve complex problems with material testing.
body_text: "Sometimes you can't just look up an answer. You're on the leading edge of understanding what's happening, and that's where the lab makes the difference." - Andy Frerichs, Senior Materials Scientist What the Corporate Materials Lab Does The CML was built to better serve customer needs related to material performance. To do that, the laboratory works across three primary areas: Internal product and process development Materials testing for new applications Direct customer support and investigation The investigation doesn't always stop at the material alone . Through an integrated approach, the CML evaluates not just the material, but the full system influencing performance - including forming conditions, processing variables, and real-world application environments. This broader perspective delivers the insight customers need to make informed decisions. "The Corporate Materials Lab is a problem-solving resource for Worthington Steel's business units and customers," Frerichs says. "We exist to help solve problems, whether they involve our material or something happening in the customer's process." "The CML is a problem-solving resource. We exist to help solve problems, whether they involve our material or something happening in the customer's process." - Andy Frerichs, Senior Materials Scientist How the CML Differs from Quality and Technical Services Customers regularly work with the quality department and metallurgical engineering teams when challenges, claims, or product development challenges, claims, or product development challenges arise. Each plays an important role. Function Primary Role Quality Verifies material meets specification Technical Services Provides customer-facing application support CML Conducts deeper technical investigation and root-cause analysis Quality confirms compliance. Technical services support the application and processing. The Corporate Materials Lab investigates when those answers don't fully explain the outcome . If the part fractures in service but passes material specification requirements such as hardness, chemistry, or other requirements, the lab examines fracture surfaces, microstructure, processing history, and application variables to uncover what standard testing may not. As George Keller, Principal Scientist and Lab Manager, puts it: "Quality measures things against a standard. We generate answers. We ask why." That investigative mindset is what sets the lab apart. Its responsibility is to uncover the root cause wherever the evidence leads. All investigations are handled under strict confidentiality protocols. When required, formal non-disclosure agreements are in place, and data is managed through secure internal systems. The lab's role is to provide technically accurate findings and maintain objectivity. How the Lab Supports Customers Customer engagement often begins with a forming inconsistency, a weld concern, a coating issue, or an unexpected variation. The CML supports customers through: Comparative material evaluations Coating and bonding analysis Validation for new or changing requirements Microstructural and metallurgical examination Weldability challenges Application-specific testing designed around real operating conditions General material performance issues, including non-steel components that interact with the steel The lab works closely with Technical Services, Quality, and manufacturing teams to ensure findings translate into practical next steps. Because the lab is embedded within Worthington Steel, investigations can begin quickly and often deliver answers within weeks rather than months. For customers managing production schedules, that speed reduces uncertainty and helps prevent extended trial-and-error cycles. When needed, members of the lab also support investigations onsite at customer or plant locations. Whether evaluating a forming issue on a production line or assisting with welding or processing studies, the team's involvement is not limited to the lab environment. When an investigation is complete, customers receive a comprehensive technical report detailing the process, testing methods, findings, and recommended next steps. As Materials Scientist Matt Duffey explains: "We are essentially researching and problem-solving across all our products and how customers use them. We understand why things may go wrong and how to overcome that so we can better serve our business units and our customers." "We understand why things may go wrong and how to overcome that so we can better serve our business units and our customers." - Matt Duffey, Materials Scientist 2 Capabilities That Enable Deeper Insight The CML brings together advanced testing equipment and expert analysis to deliver accurate results. Capabilities include: Microscopic and microstructural analysis Tensile and mechanical testing Grain structure and directional property evaluation Coating and bonding assessment Access to specialized external laboratories when required Tools such as scanning electron microscopy enable the team to examine fracture surfaces and micro-level features that are invisible in routine testing. A typical investigation may begin with visual and mechanical evaluation, move into microstructural analysis, and expand into surface or bonding studies, depending on early findings. Each step builds a clearer understanding of how the material behaves in science. When specialized analysis is required, the lab collaborates with trusted external partners to ensure complete answers. The People Behind the Lab The strength of the Corporate Materials Lab lies in its team's experience. The group includes specialists in failure analysis, welding, metallurgical behavior, coatings, forming performance, chemistry, mechanical testing, materials processing, and advanced materials characterization. Their backgrounds span production, research, product development, and field troubleshooting. That breadth matters. A welding issue may require metallurgical insight. A forming concern may be traced back to microstructure. A coating problem can originate upstream in processing conditions. As Frerichs explains: "Between the experience on this team and the different technical backgrounds we have, we're able to look at a problem from several perspectives and narrow in on what's really driving it." Why This Matters When performance questions arise, time and certainty matter. Extended trial-and-error cycles increase cost. Unsolved questions can create risk. The Corporate Materials Lab provides a structured investigation that reduces uncertainty and protects operational stability . Customers gain a clear understanding of what happened, why it happened, and what steps to take next. Many companies focus primarily on processing and certification. Worthington Steel has invested in deeper technical capability to position itself as a problem-solving partner, not simply a material supplier. When steel questions get complicated, Worthington Steel doesn't guess. It investigates. And that makes the difference. About Worthington Steel Since 1955, Worthington Flat Roll Steel has been delivering top-quality service that enables our customers to do the same for themselves. Our steel processing capabilities serve a variety of markets, including automotive , heavy truck , agriculture , energy , construction , and many others. Our commitment to our customers' business goes far beyond supplying steel. We provide advanced materials support , buying strategies , supply chain solutions , and the highest level of customer service and collaboration. If you are interested in learning more about us at Worthington Steel, want to view our capabilities , or have a question that we can help you answer , please explore our website or call us at 1.800.944.3733. We are here to be partners for your manufacturing goals.

title: Chase Virtual Card Number: How to Get One Today | Grey
summary: Need a Chase virtual card number? Learn how to generate one in the Chase app, where you can use it, and the best alternatives. Start shopping safely today.
body_text: If you shop online regularly, you have probably wondered what happens to your card number after entering it at a payment checkout and how safe it is. Even recently, Chick-fil-A and Origin Energy reported breaches that exposed customers’ contact details and partial card numbers. A virtual card number helps reduce that risk by replacing your real card details with a temporary one. A Chase virtual card number is a temporary card number generated in the Chase mobile app for eligible Chase cards. It lets you shop online without exposing your real card number. To get one, open the Chase app, select your eligible card, tap "Account services" and then "Virtual card number." The virtual number works at most online merchants. Whether you're shopping with a retailer for the first time, signing up for a free trial, or simply want an extra layer of security, this guide explains how Chase virtual card numbers work, which cards support them, how to generate one, and the best alternatives if your card isn't eligible. What is a Chase virtual card number? A Chase virtual card number is a temporary card number linked to your eligible Chase card account. You use this temporary number when shopping online instead of your actual card number. The merchant processes the payment normally, but your real card number is never shared. Since the merchants never receive your real card details, virtual card numbers add an extra layer of protection against data breaches and card fraud. If the merchant has a breach and the virtual number gets compromised, your physical card number remains hidden. So, your money and account are safe. According to Chase's official website , the virtual card numbers feature is only available for eligible Chase cards through the Chase mobile app. The temporary number is linked to your real account for just that transaction, so it appears like a normal transaction on your bank statement Eligible cards include: Chase Sapphire Preferred and Sapphire Reserve Chase Freedom Flex and Freedom Unlimited Chase Ink Business cards (selected products) Other selected Chase Visa and Mastercard cards Open the Chase app to check your card type and confirm if the feature is available for your account and card. How to get a Chase virtual card If your card is eligible, generating a Chase virtual card barely takes two minutes once you are in the app. Here is how to get a Chase virtual card from your Chase app: Open the Chase mobile app and log in to your account. Select the card you want to generate a virtual number for. Make sure it is an eligible card. You will see this option if it is supported. Tap "Account services." This is usually accessible from the card's main screen or the menu. Tap "Virtual card number." If your card is eligible, this option appears. If it isn't there, your card doesn't currently support the feature. Review the virtual card details. Chase displays the temporary card number, expiry date, and CVV. These details replace your real card information at checkout. Copy the details or use them directly. When checking out online, enter the virtual number, expiry, and CVV in place of your real card information. The virtual number expires after some time or once you have used it. If you need a new one, simply generate another virtual card number in the app. Using a Chase virtual card for online shopping Virtual card numbers are particularly useful in three situations. Subscriptions on new platforms If you have ever forgotten to cancel a subscription and got charged, you should understand why a virtual card number is a good idea. When signing up for a subscription on a service you have not used before, using a virtual number means your real card is not stored by that service. So, if you decide to cancel, you do not have to update your card details everywhere. One-off purchases from unfamiliar stores If you are buying from a smaller retailer or a site you have not used before, a virtual number limits your exposure if the site ever gets compromised. Signing up for free trials Using a virtual card number is a hack when trying to sign up for free trials, and you don’t want to be charged automatically when the trial ends. A virtual card number expires either when you use it or after some time. This means the charge does not go through if you forget to cancel. Once you have generated the number and you are at the checkout page, here’s what to enter: The virtual card number in the card number field The virtual expiry date in the expiry field The virtual CVV in the security code field. The billing address is the same as the one on your real Chase account. Do not enter the actual card details printed on your physical Chase card! How to pay with a Chase virtual card There isn't much difference between paying with your physical card and paying with a Chase virtual card. The steps are similar; you are just entering a virtual number instead of your real card number. Step 1: At the checkout page, select "Credit/debit card" or "Pay by card" as the payment method. Step 2: Enter the virtual card number, expiry date, and CVV from the Chase app. Again, do not enter the details on your physical card. Step 3: Enter your billing address as registered with Chase. Step 4: Complete the purchase. If your payment is declined If your virtual card number doesn’t work on a platform, if might be because some merchants don’t accept tokenised or virtual card numbers. This is more common with: Merchants that verify the card number against a specific format Hotels or rental car companies that need to hold a card for incidentals Some subscription platforms that require a card to be stored long-term If a virtual number is rejected, you can try again with your real card number for that specific merchant. Chase virtual card limitations While Chase virtual card numbers can be very useful, they come with some limitations. Only available for eligible cards: Not all Chase cards support virtual card numbers. If the option does not appear in your app, your card does not have this feature yet. They are designed for online purchases: Virtual card numbers are for online purchases only. They cannot be used if you are buying from a physical store or using an ATM. Some merchants do not accept them: Hotels, car rental companies, and certain subscription services may require your physical card instead. Foreign transaction fees still apply: A virtual card doesn't remove the foreign transaction fees charged by your Chase card when shopping with overseas merchants. Alternatives to Chase virtual cards Chase is not the only provider of virtual or temporary card numbers for online shopping. Several banks and fintech platforms offer similar (and in some cases more flexible) tools that protect your real card details while giving you greater control over spending limits, merchant locks, and currency support. Other bank virtual cards Many major US banks provide their own versions of virtual card numbers: Capital One Eno generates unique virtual numbers that can be locked to a specific merchant and set with spending limits or expiration dates. Citi Virtual Account Numbers let you create temporary numbers tied to your existing Citi credit card. American Express and some Bank of America products also offer virtual card features on select accounts. These options work best if you already bank with one of these institutions and primarily shop in US dollars. They keep everything inside your existing credit relationship and usually require no extra account setup. The main limitation is that they are tied to a single currency (almost always USD) and are primarily designed for customers with US residency and a traditional credit card. Fintech virtual cards Fintech platforms go further by letting you create virtual cards that draw from multi-currency balances rather than a single-currency account. For example, Grey lets users hold USD, EUR, or GBP balances in one account and generate virtual cards that spend directly from those balances. This is particularly useful for: Paying for international subscriptions (AWS, ChatGPT, Adobe, Facebook Ads, etc.) Shopping on US or European websites while living outside the US Avoiding repeated currency conversion every time you make a purchase Grey users can create multiple cards for various reasons, freeze or delete a card instantly, and integrate with Apple Pay and Google Pay for contactless payment. Because the card is funded from a multi-currency balance, you control when you convert money into the currency you need to spend. A one-time card creation fee of $5 applies. Other fintech options, such as Wise and Revolut, also offer virtual or disposable cards depending on the location and currency. Here is a summary explaining when each option is the better fit: Situation Better choice Why You already have a Chase credit card and mostly shop in USD Chase (or Click to Pay) Simple, no new account needed You bank with Capital One, Citi, or Amex and want merchant-locked numbers Capital One Eno / Citi / Amex Strong native controls inside your existing bank You need to hold and spend in USD, EUR, or GBP Grey Multi-currency balances + virtual cards linked directly to those balances You live outside the US or earn in foreign currencies Grey or similar fintech Avoids reliance on a US credit history or traditional bank account You want maximum disposable / single-use cards Privacy.com or similar Designed for high-volume temporary numbers See also how Mastercard virtual cards work for a broader comparison of virtual card types. Chase virtual card numbers (where available) remain convenient for existing customers who stay within the US banking system. Traditional bank alternatives work well if you prefer everything under one credit card relationship. Fintech solutions like Grey become a stronger fit when multi-currency flexibility, international online shopping, or the ability to spend from held foreign balances matter more than staying inside a single US credit product. Get a Grey virtual card and manage international purchases without manual top-ups and currency conversion. Frequently asked questions Which Chase cards have virtual card numbers? Chase Sapphire Preferred, Chase Sapphire Reserve, Chase Freedom Flex, Chase Freedom Unlimited, and selected Chase Ink Business cards currently support virtual card numbers. The easiest way to check is to open your card in the Chase mobile app and look for the "Virtual card number" option under Account services. If the option isn't there, your card isn't currently eligible. Does the Chase virtual card number change? Yes. Chase generates a new virtual card number each time you request one. The number is temporary and typically expires after a defined period or number of uses. This is a security feature: an expiring number limits how useful it is to anyone who obtains it without your consent. Can I use a Chase virtual card abroad? You can use a Chase virtual card number for purchases on foreign websites where you pay online. However, if the purchase is in a foreign currency, the same foreign transaction fees that apply to your physical Chase card also apply to the virtual number. Virtual card numbers do not remove foreign transaction fees. Does a Chase virtual card work for subscriptions? It depends on how the subscription platform handles card validation. Some subscription services accept tokenised numbers and can charge them repeatedly. Others require a long-term card on file and may have issues with numbers that expire. For subscriptions, check whether the virtual number is locked to a single transaction or can be used for recurring charges. What is the best multi-currency alternative to a Chase virtual card? For shoppers who purchase in multiple currencies or need a virtual card that works independently of an existing US bank account, the Grey Plus Card is a strong option. It is a virtual Visa card connected to USD, GBP, or EUR balances, with no foreign transaction fee for same-currency purchases, and it works in any browser on any device. How do I get a Grey virtual card? Sign up at grey.co and complete identity verification. Open a USD, GBP, or EUR account. Navigate to the Cards section and create the Grey virtual card. A one-time $5 creation fee applies. Card details are available immediately in the app and ready to enter at any online checkout.

title: Back-to-school shopping trends: How AI is reshaping the season for brands | Criteo
summary: Here are the most important back-to-school shopping trends as we head into the new school year with AI advertising at the centerfold.
body_text: Table of contents Trend #1: Discovery starts earlier—and increasingly with AI Trend #2: The path to purchase is becoming more connected Trend #3: Commerce data matters more than ever Trend #4: Small teams are using AI to compete more effectively Preparing for the future of back-to-school shopping What are the biggest back-to-school shopping trends this year? How is AI changing back-to-school advertising? Why is cross-channel advertising important during back-to-school? How can small businesses use AI for back-to-school marketing? See what Criteo GO can do for your business Back-to-school shopping has always been one of retail’s biggest moments, but the way shoppers prepare for it is changing. Back-to-school shopping no longer follows a predictable path. A single purchase might begin with an AI recommendation, continue with product reviews on social media, move to price comparisons across retailers, and end days later on a completely different device. As shoppers discover, research, and buy in more ways than ever before, the moments that influence a purchase are expanding beyond the traditional search engine or retailer website. This year, one trend stands above the rest: AI is changing how shoppers discover products. Instead of beginning with a search, more consumers are turning to AI to ask questions, compare options, and narrow their choices before they ever visit a retailer’s website. In fact, 47% of shoppers now use AI to research and compare products, while 39% use it to discover new products and recommendations. That shift is creating new opportunities for brands to connect with shoppers earlier in the journey—and changing what it takes to stand out during one of the busiest shopping seasons of the year. Trend #1: Discovery starts earlier—and increasingly with AI For years, marketers have focused on capturing demand once shoppers knew what they wanted. Someone searched for “best backpack for middle school,” clicked an ad, and eventually made a purchase. Today, those journeys often begin much earlier. Instead of searching for a product, shoppers are asking broader questions. A parent might ask AI what supplies a first grader actually needs. A college student might ask for the best laptop for an engineering program within a certain budget. A teacher might ask how to stretch a classroom supply budget without sacrificing quality. These aren’t traditional product searches. They’re conversations that combine discovery and evaluation into a single experience. By the time shoppers arrive on a retailer’s website, many have already narrowed their options. Criteo’s data shows that shoppers referred by AI convert at 1.5x the rate of those referred by traditional search , highlighting how AI is helping consumers make more informed decisions before they ever click through to a retailer. For marketers, it’s a reminder that discovery is no longer confined to the top of the funnel. Increasingly, it’s becoming one of the strongest drivers of performance. Trend #2: The path to purchase is becoming more connected Back-to-school shopping rarely happens in one sitting. A shopper might discover a product recommendation through AI, watch reviews on social media during lunch, compare prices on a retailer’s website that evening, and complete the purchase a few days later after seeing another reminder on the open web. Rather than moving through a neat, linear funnel, shoppers move fluidly between channels depending on what they need at that moment. This makes consistency more important than ever. Showing up across multiple touchpoints helps reinforce your message while giving shoppers the confidence to return when they’re ready to buy. Instead of thinking about awareness, consideration, and conversion as separate campaigns, marketers increasingly need to connect those experiences into one cohesive strategy. That shift is also influencing brand preference. According to eMarketer , nearly half of shoppers say they would consider a different brand or product if an AI assistant recommended an alternative. For marketers, that means the opportunity to influence purchasing decisions begins well before a shopper types a keyword into a search engine—particularly important for brands trying to market during compressed purchasing windows like back-to-school season. Trend #3: Commerce data matters more than ever AI is transforming advertising, but the quality of its recommendations depends on the quality of the data behind them. Back-to-school shopping behavior changes quickly. Product demand shifts from backpacks and notebooks to laptops, calculators, dorm essentials, and classroom supplies as the season progresses. Consumer priorities also change as budgets tighten, promotions launch, and inventory fluctuates. Keeping up with those shifts manually is difficult for even the largest marketing teams. AI that is rooted in commerce, or purchasing, data helps simplify that process by using real shopping signals to continuously optimize campaign performance. Rather than relying solely on broad audience assumptions or historical behavior, it can respond to how shoppers are actively discovering and evaluating products throughout the season. For growing businesses with limited time and resources, that means spending less time making manual adjustments and more time focusing on promotions, creative, and customer experience. Trend #4: Small teams are using AI to compete more effectively One of the biggest misconceptions about AI advertising is that it’s only useful or scalable for large brands with dedicated marketing teams. In reality, AI may have the biggest impact for small businesses. Launching and managing campaigns across multiple advertising platforms has become increasingly complex. Every platform has its own workflows, reporting, and optimization tools, making it difficult for lean teams to keep up—especially during seasonal peaks like back-to-school. That’s where self-service platforms like Criteo GO can help. Built with the same commerce expertise that powers Criteo’s Commerce Growth solutions, Criteo GO helps businesses drive discovery, acquire new customers, and maximize conversions without adding unnecessary complexity. Its AI-assisted onboarding makes it easy to get started, while Commerce AI continuously optimizes targeting, bidding, and creative using real-time commerce signals. Instead of managing separate campaigns across multiple platforms, marketers can reach shoppers across the open web, social, video, apps, and emerging environments like ChatGPT from one place. That simplicity allows small teams to compete more effectively during one of retail’s most important seasons. Preparing for the future of back-to-school shopping Every year brings new back-to-school shopping trends, but this year’s biggest shift isn’t a new product category or another social platform. It’s the way shoppers are making buying decisions online. AI is changing how people discover products, compare options, and build confidence before they buy. As discovery becomes more conversational and the path to purchase becomes more connected, brands have an opportunity to engage shoppers earlier than ever before. The businesses that succeed won’t necessarily be the ones with the largest advertising budgets. They’ll be the ones that understand how shoppers are changing and adapt their marketing strategies accordingly. For growing businesses, that means embracing AI not as another marketing channel, but as a smarter way to reach customers across the channels they’re already using. Frequently asked questions What are the biggest back-to-school shopping trends this year? One of the biggest trends is the growing role of AI in product discovery. Shoppers are increasingly using AI to research products, compare options, and make purchasing decisions before they visit a retailer’s website. At the same time, shoppers continue to move across multiple channels throughout their buying journey, making cross-channel advertising more important than ever. How is AI changing back-to-school advertising? AI is helping brands reach shoppers earlier in the customer journey while also improving campaign performance through automated optimization. By using commerce signals to optimize targeting, bidding, and creative, AI can help marketers adapt more quickly to changing shopper behavior throughout the season. Why is cross-channel advertising important during back-to-school? Back-to-school shoppers rarely rely on a single channel. They may discover products through AI, browse on social media, compare options on retailer websites, and purchase after seeing additional ads on the open web. A cross-channel strategy helps brands stay visible throughout those moments instead of relying on a single touchpoint. How can small businesses use AI for back-to-school marketing? AI-powered advertising platforms like Criteo GO help small businesses launch campaigns quickly, automate optimization, and reach shoppers across multiple channels without requiring extensive marketing resources. That allows lean teams to spend less time managing campaigns and more time growing their business. title: Doximity to Release Fiscal 2022 Third Quarter Results on February 8, 2022
summary: Doximity Press Releases
body_text: SAN FRANCISCO, Jan. 18, 2022/ /PRNewswire/ -- Doximity, Inc.
